Chromatography in which the composition of the mobile phase remains constant during elution.

comments: The column radius \(r_{\rm{c}} = d_{\rm{c}}/2\).

basicPropertyValues.val: Inner diameter of the column tubing.
Length of that part of the column tube that contains the stationary phase.
Cross-sectional area of the empty tube: \(A_{\rm{c}} = \pi r_{\rm{c}}^{2} = \pi (d_{\rm{c}}/2)^{2}\), where \(d_{\rm{c}}\) is the column diameter.
Average thickness of the liquid stationary phase film coated on the inside wall of the column tubing of an open-tubular column.
Column packed with a single piece of solid material (monolith) composed of interconnected skeletons (forming macropores) and interconnected flow paths (mesopores) as a stationary phase material.

comments: For a symmetrical peak \(A_{\rm{s}} = 1\).
Some pharmacopoeia definitions of peak asymmetry measure the value at \(\pu{5\%}\) of the peak height.

basicPropertyValues.val: Width of a peak (\(f + b\)) divided by twice the width of the front of the peak (\(f\)), measured at \(\pu{10\%}\) of the peak height (see figure). \[A_{\rm{s}} = \frac{(f + b)}{2f}\] Peak asymmetry (schematic). \(R_{\rm{D}}\) is the response of the detector.Peak asymmetry (schematic). \(R_{\rm{D}}\) is the response of the detector.
Peak width at peak base intercepted by tangents to the chromatogram drawn at the inflection points on either side of the peak. Represented by the line AB in the peak height figure.

comments: The peak width at half height must never be called the "half width" because that has a completely different meaning.
The peak width at half height of a Gaussian peak is about 2.355 times the standard deviation of the modelled Gaussian. See figure in peak height.

basicPropertyValues.val: Peak width at \(\pu{50\%}\) of the peak height that terminates at the intersections with the peak.
Width of the back of a peak (\(b\)) divided by the width of the front (\(f\)) of the peak measured at \(\pu{10\%}\) of the peak height. See figure in asymmetry factor.

synonyms.val: height equivalent to one effective plate

basicPropertyValues.val: Column length (\(L\)) divided by effective plate number (\(N_{\rm{eff}}\)): \[H_{\rm{eff}} = \frac{L}{N_{\rm{eff}}}\]

comments: The plate number is related to the effective plate number and retention factor (\(k\)) \(N = N_{\rm{eff}}{\left(\frac{{k + 1}}{k} \right)^2}\)
These expressions assume a Gaussian (symmetrical) peak.
Units for the quantities being divided must be consistent so that their ratio is dimensionless: i.e. if the numerator is a time, then peak width must also be expressed in terms of time

\(V_{\rm{R}}^{\prime}\): adjusted retention volume; \(t_{\rm{R}}^{\prime}\): total retention time; \(\sigma\): standard deviation of the Gaussian peak; \(w_{\rm{b}}\): peak width at base; \(w_{\rm{h}}\): peak width at half height; \(\rm{8 \ln 2} ≈ 5.545\).

basicPropertyValues.val: Number indicative of column performance, calculated from the ratios of measures of adjusted retention and peak width: \[\eqalign{& N_{\rm{eff}} = \left(\frac{V_{\rm{R}}^{\prime}}{\sigma} \right)^{2} = \left(\frac{t_{\rm{R}}^{\prime}}{\sigma} \right)^{2} \cr & N_{\rm{eff}} = 16 \left(\frac{V_{\rm{R}}^{\prime}}{w_{\rm{b}}} \right)^{2} = 16 \left(\frac{t_{\rm{R}}^{\prime}}{w_{\rm{b}}} \right)^{2} \cr & N_{\rm{eff}} \approx 5.545 \left(\frac{V_{\rm{R}}^{\prime}}{w_{\rm{h}}} \right)^{2} \approx 5.545 \left(\frac{t_{\rm{R}}^{\prime}}{w_{\rm{h}}} \right)^{2}}\]

comments: For open-tubular columns \(h\) is the plate height divided by the column diameter, \(h = H/d_{\rm{c}}\).

basicPropertyValues.val: In liquid chromatography plate height divided by average particle diameter. \[h = H/d_{\rm{p}}\]
Sensor that responds to components in the effluent.

comments: Biospecific compounds can be already in the sample (receptor-acceptor formation under applied electric field, or the bioselective compounds may be attached on the capillary inner wall before the analysis starts. They are bound covalently or dynamically on the surface.

basicPropertyValues.val: Capillary electrophoresis in which the background electrolyte contains substances capable of specific, often biospecific, interactions with the analytes.

comments: The retention time is determined by a combination of electrophoretic migration and chromatographic retention.

basicPropertyValues.val: Liquid chromatography, where the movement of the mobile phase through a capillary, filled, packed, or coated with a stationary phase, is achieved by electroosmotic flow (which may be assisted by pressure).

comments: The background electrolyte may be an aqueous or non-aqueous solution.

The basic kind of CE is capillary zone electrophoresis in which separation takes place in the homogeneous solution of the background electrolyte on the basis of different electrophoretic mobilities of analytes in a free solution.
The electrolytes can contain additives, which can interact with the charged species and alter their electrophoretic mobilities.

The use of the term capillary electrophoresis (CE) as a collective term for all capillary electromigration techniques is not recommended, as some of these techniques involve separation mechanisms other than electrophoresis.

basicPropertyValues.val: Separation method based solely on the differences in the electrophoretic mobilities of charged species in capillaries.
Capillary sieving electrophoresis in which the capillary is filled with a gel.
Electrophoretic technique for the separation of analytes according to their isoelectric points by an electric field along a pH gradient formed in a capillary.

Electrophoretic separation technique in a discontinuous buffer system in which analytes migrate according to their electrophoretic mobilities, forming a chain of adjacent zones moving with equal speed (velocity) between two solutions, leading and terminating electrolytes, bracketing the mobility range of the analytes.

comments: The medium may be an entangled polymer network.

basicPropertyValues.val: Electrophoretic separation technique, which takes place in a capillary containing a medium in the background electrolyte that retains molecules and particles based on their size and shape.
Length of the capillary from the sample introduction point to the detection point.

comments: This is not totally compatible with the definition of chromatography.
Surfactants must be at concentrations above their critical micelle concentration for being able to form a dispersed phase – otherwise they will just act as ion-pair reagents.

basicPropertyValues.val: Separation method based on a combination of electrophoresis and interactions of the analytes with additives (e.g. surfactants), which form a dispersed phase moving at a different speed (velocity). In order to achieve separation, either the analytes or this secondary phase should be charged.

Injection of the analytical sample by applying a potential across the sample and capillary and using the electroosmotic flow to draw an aliquot into the end of the capillary tube. The sample is then replaced by the running electrolyte for the separation to take place.
Motion of a liquid through a capillary (or membrane or plug) because of the application of an electric field across the capillary (or membrane or plug).

comments: In capillary electromigration, this velocity is positive, by convention, in the direction from the sample introduction end of the capillary to the detection end, otherwise negative.

basicPropertyValues.val: Effective length of the capillary (\(L_{\rm{eff}}\)) divided by the electroosmotic hold-up time (\(t_{\rm{eo}}\)). \[\boldsymbol{v}_{\rm{eo}} = L_{\rm{eff}}/t_{\rm{eo}}\]
Volume flow rate divided by electric field strength through the whole plug or capillary.

comments: Electrostacking methods can be used to concentrate dilute samples.

basicPropertyValues.val: Methods that use differences in migration behaviour in spatially defined regions of the capillary of different field strengths (conductivities).
Introduction of the analytical sample into a capillary by a pressure difference between the ends of the capillary.
Biochemical methods for separation and characterization of proteins based on electrophoresis and reaction with antibodies.
Electrokinetic chromatography, in which the secondary phase is a micellar dispersed phase in the capillary.
Electrokinetic chromatography, where a microemulsion is employed as the dispersed phase.

comments: Typical modifiers are acetic acid, sodium acetate, ammonium acetate, ammonium chloride and ammonium hydroxide (non aqueous).
Typical organic solvents are methanol, ethanol, propanol, and acetonitrile.

basicPropertyValues.val: Capillary electrophoresis, which uses water-free organic solutions and modifiers to produce ions in solution.

comments: Usually, the leading and terminating electrolytes have a common counter-ion, but the co-ions are different.

basicPropertyValues.val: In isotachophoresis a sample is introduced between a zone of fast leading electrolyte and a zone of slow terminating electrolyte.

comments: Advantages of AsFlFFF include that the upper channel wall can be made of a transparent material, allowing the accumulation and sample migration to be viewed. Sample focusing can be achieved during relaxation, resulting in a narrower sample band being produced, resulting in lower band broadening.

In a uniform width channel this would result in the channel flow decreasing dramatically along the channel length. In order to minimize this, a trapezoid shape of the separation channel has been developed for AsFlFFF. In general, the channel geometry significantly affects the separation efficiency in AF4.

Three different channel designs were evaluated using polystyrene latex nanoparticles. The channel breadth was held constant for one (rectangular) profile, and was reduced either linearly (trapezoid profile) or exponentially (exponential profile) along the length for the other two channels. Com-pared with a rectangular channel, trapezoid and exponential profiles provided better performance of AsFlFFF and allowed band broadening to be reduced.

basicPropertyValues.val: Flow field-flow fractionation in which only one channel wall is permeable, meaning there is one channel inlet for the flow during the run and some of the channel flow is directed through the accumulation wall.

comments: BFFF mode requires a specific sample injection procedure described as stop-flow injection or a relaxation step. A relaxation time is needed to equilibrate the sample under the influence of a force field and Brownian diffusion in the absence of flow. The injected sample is forced to concentrate in a thin layer adjacent to the accumulation wall (channel bottom).
Two main factors influencing the sample behaviour in BFFF mode are the properties of particles characterized by the diffusion coefficient and the strength of the cross-field applied.

When the flow is switched on, elution begins with smaller particles, which are distributed further away from the accumulation wall and thus protrude further into the faster flow streams; larger particles elute later.

basicPropertyValues.val: Mechanism of field-flow fractionation of sub-micron particles that relies on Brownian motion.

comments: CTFFF can be attributed to non-conventional sedimentation field-flow fractionation (SdFFF), which enables the sample mass to be increased to gram levels.
The complex asymmetrical force field is generated in planetary centrifuges where the column drum rotates around its own axis and at the same time revolves around the central axis of the centrifuge.

basicPropertyValues.val: Field-flow fractionation in a long (usually \(\pu{10 m}\) or more) rotating coiled column under the action of asymmetrical centrifugal field.

comments: Although similar to liquid chromatography, FFF requires no stationary phase, so the separation channel contains no packing material and only physical interactions are involved in the separation process.
FFF is applicable to the fractionation and characterization of colloidal and solid particles, polymers, and biological cells in the size range from \(\pu{1 nm}\) to \(\pu{50 \upmu m}\).
The sample mass injected is usually less than \(\pu{1 mg}\) to avoid overloading.

basicPropertyValues.val: Separation based on the retention and elution of macromolecular, colloidal, and particulate matter achieved by the combined action of the non-uniform flow speed (velocity) profile of a carrier fluid (mobile phase) and a physical force field (e.g. gravitational, centrifugal, electrical) applied at right angles to a thin (\(\pu{0.05 mm}\) to \(\pu{0.5 mm}\)) channel (see figure). Basic principle of field-flow fractionation.Basic principle of field-flow fractionation.

comments: Like sedimentation field-flow fractionation (SdFFF), FlFFF can be used for submicron particles and macromolecules using the Brownian field-flow fractionation mode or micron size particles utilizing the hyperlayer mode.
The sample components are driven by the cross-flow toward the accumulation wall, which consists of porous frit covered with a permeable membrane.

This technique can be applied to the size fractionation of different synthetic polymers, liposomes, proteins, viruses, dissolved organic matter, humic and fulvic acids as well as their complexes with trace metals, diesel soot particles, marine colloids, heterogeneous and arbitrarily shaped natural colloidal particles, gold colloid standards starting from 5 nm.

basicPropertyValues.val: Field-flow fractionation in which the physical force field is a nonspecific hydrodynamic force field across the channel, generated by a secondary mobile phase cross-flow in addition to the normal channel flow.

comments: GFFF can fractionate particulate matter in the micrometre size range (large microorganisms, blood cells, sediments, etc).

Since the Earth’s gravitational field produces relatively weak forces, this mode is only appropriate for micron size particles, hence the separation is an example of hyperlayer focusing field-flow fractionation.

basicPropertyValues.val: Field-flow fractionation in which the physical force field is the Earth’s gravitational field.

comments: Due to the large size of the particles, Brownian diffusion away from the accumulation wall is assumed to be negligible in this mode.

HyFFF is a preferred alternative to steric field-flow fractionation. The retention of particles larger than \(\pu{1 \upmu m}\) typically increases with flow rate. Particles are driven away from the wall by a hydrody-namic lift force and elevated into faster flow streams. The particles form thin layers at an equilibrium position, where the external field is balanced by the opposing hydrodynamic lift force, as compared to steric mode, where the thin layer of particles is adjacent to the accumulation wall.

basicPropertyValues.val: Mechanism of field-flow fractionation of particles greater than \(\pu{1 \upmu m}\) in diameter relying on hydrodynamic lift forces near the channel wall to move particles into faster flowing streams.

comments: SdFFF can be applied to a wide range of colloidal and micron size particles and is a powerful method for cell separations, including industrial carbon blacks, silica nanoparticles, silver and gold nano-particles, aquatic sediments, aerosols, and latex beads.

SdFFF can be successfully applied to the fractionation and characterization (sizing) of submicron particles, starting from about \(\pu{5 nm}\), but this limit depends on the particle density, as the separation is based on the buoyant mass of the particles.

SdFFF can operate in both the Brownian field-flow fractionation (BFFF) and hyperlayer field-flow fractionation (HyFFF) modes and caution must be exercised if samples span the Brownian-hyperlayer transition point of about \(\pu{1 \upmu m}\), as this can lead to separated fractions containing two particle sizes, smaller particles separated by Brownian mode and larger particles separated by hyperlayer mode.
SdFFF is performed in a circular flat channel inserted inside a centrifugal basket.

basicPropertyValues.val: Field-flow fractionation in which the physical force field is a centrifugal force field.

comments: A semi-preparative binary separation can be generated with smaller particles eluting from one outlet and larger particles emerging from the other. Careful manipulation of the inlet and outlet flow rates and the field strength enables the cut-off diameter of the particles to be selected.
Although SPILTT is similar to field-flow fractionation, it should not be referred to as FFF. The separation is achieved by the combined action of controlled flow rates and an applied cross-field.
Fields that have been tested so far include gravitational, centrifugal and magnetic.
SPLITT enables the separation of samples of masses of the order of grams.

The system has two channel inlets and two outlets. Sample suspension is continuously pumped into one inlet and carrier liquid is pumped into the other inlet. Due to the laminar flow conditions, these two streams do not mix.

basicPropertyValues.val: Separation in which laminar flow conditions are established between a liquid containing suspended sample and a carrier liquid, with a physical force field applied across the streams.

comments: In StFFF the elution order is opposite to that of Brownian field-flow fractionation mode and larger particles move ahead of smaller ones.

It was originally considered that particles are in contact with the accumulation wall during the entire migration time and consequently the centre of larger particles are situated closer to the centre of the channel in the faster flow streams. This is never achieved in practice due to hydrodynamic lift forces away from the accumulation wall.

basicPropertyValues.val: Mechanism of field-flow fractionation of particles greater than \(\pu{1 \upmu m}\) in diameter relying on proximity to the accumulation wall.

comments: The width is constant except for triangular sections at each of the ends of the channel.
Theory and data analysis are simplified by the assumption of constant flow.

basicPropertyValues.val: Flow field-flow fractionation in which the speed of mobile phase is constant along the length of the channel due to constant channel width.

comments: One side of the channel is heated and the other side is cooled. A relatively small temperature difference between the top and bottom walls of the channel provides a high thermal gradient.

TFFF has been mainly used for the separation of lyophilic synthetic polymers, including ultrahigh molecular weight polymers and microgels. However, some reports of other types of macromolecules and particles, including aqueous solvents, are present in the literature.

basicPropertyValues.val: Field-flow fractionation in which the physical force field is created by a temperature difference across the channel.

Method of introduction of the mobile phase (upper or lower) into the rotating coil (from the head or the tail). Of four combinations, only two elution modes should be used in high-speed counter-current chromatography, i.e. either the lower phase from the head toward the tail or the upper phase from the tail toward the head.

comments: The method covers analytical (microgram) to preparative (\(\pu{10 g}\)) scale separations usually in a few hours at a high partition efficiency up to a few thousand theoretical plates (see number of theoretical plates).

basicPropertyValues.val: Counter-current chromatography system using a multilayer coil separation column, which undergoes a type-J synchronous planetary motion (see figure).Type-J planetary motion of a multilayer coil separation column. The column holder rotates about its own axis and revolves around the centrifuge axis at the same angular velocity (ω) in the same direction. This planetary motion prevents twisting of the bundle of flow tubes, allowing continuous elution through a rotating column without risk of leakage and contamination.

Volume of the liquid mobile phase contained in the column in counter-current chromatography \[V_{\rm{M}} = V_{\rm{C}} - V_{\rm{S}}\] where \(V_{\rm{C}}\) is the total volume of the column and \(V_{\rm{S}}\) is the volume of the liquid stationary phase in the column.

comments: The multilayer coil is prepared from a long piece of polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) tubing by coaxially winding it around a spool-shaped holder, making multiple coiled layers.

Usually, three different inner diameter sizes of tubing are used: ca. \(\pu{1 mm}\) for analytical, \(\pu{1.6 mm}\) for semipreparative, and \(\pu{2.6 mm}\) for preparative separations. It provides efficient mixing of the two phases and a high retention of the stationary phase under a high flow rate of the mobile phase.

basicPropertyValues.val: Separation column used for high-speed counter-current chromatography.

Counter-current chromatography that produces a train of fused rectangular solute peaks called pH-zones, each with its specific pH. Each zone contains highly concentrated solute, often near saturation level, and is separated from the neighbouring zone by a narrow strip called a mixing zone, which contains a mixture of impurities.

comments: Trifluoroacetic acid and triethylamine are typical retainers for the separation of acidic and basic compounds, respectively, where the stationary phase typically is the organic phase. The retainer determines the analyte concentration in the stationary phase. NH4OH and HCl are commonly used as the eluter for the separation of acidic and basic compounds, respectively. The eluter always stays in the aqueous mobile phase to serve as a counter ion. pH-zone-refining CCC can also be performed using the organic phase as the mobile phase (normal displacement mode). In this case, the retainer becomes the eluter to elute the analytes, and the eluter becomes the retainer to retain the analytes in the aqueous stationary phase.

basicPropertyValues.val: Most important reagents in pH-zone-refining counter-current chromatography. A retainer is added to the stationary organic phase to retain the analytes and the eluter added to the mobile aqueous phase to elute the analytes.

nodes.lbl: retention volume of the stationary phase

comments: \(V_{\rm{s}}\) is one of the most important parameters that determines the peak resolution.

basicPropertyValues.val: Volume of the stationary phase, which stays permanently within the column in counter-current chromatography.
Centrifuge that provides type-J synchronous planetary motion to the column holder, the axis of which is parallel to the centrifuge axis (see figure in high-speed counter-current chromatography).

comments: The system prevents the flow tubes from twisting during column rotation, and produces an excellent mixing and high retention of the stationary phase in a multilayer coil separation column.

basicPropertyValues.val: Unique type of planetary motion (so named because the flow tubes form a letter J figure, as shown in the figure in high-speed counter-current chromatography) of the column holder, which rotates around its own axis once during one revolution around the central axis of the centrifuge in the same direction.
Chiral selector that has been added as a component of a mobile phase or electrophoretic medium.

comments: The multiplier (\(\times\)) is used to denote the two separation steps, e.g. \(GC \times GC\) or \(LC \times SFC\) .

basicPropertyValues.val: Type of two-dimensional chromatography in which all the effluent from the first separation step is transferred in fractions to a second separation step.
Type of two-dimensional chromatography in which selected fractions from the first separation step are transferred to a second separation step.
Number of modulations in a given time interval.
Number of modulations for a given first-dimension peak.

comments: Modulation period is the length of a second-dimension chromatogram, i.e. the time between two successive injections into the second column.

basicPropertyValues.val: Duration of a complete cycle of modulation in a system for comprehensive two-dimensional chromatography.

Interface device between the two columns in a system for comprehensive two-dimensional chromatography that accumulates or samples narrow bands from the effluent of the first column for fast re-injection into the second column.

comments: Multi-dimensional chromatography can be done, for example, by conducting a particular fraction eluting from the column into other columns (system) having different separation characteristics.

basicPropertyValues.val: Chromatography in which parts or all of the separated sample components are subjected to additional separation steps.
Occurrence of second dimension peaks in subsequent elution sequences, caused by second-dimension retention times that exceed the modulation time in comprehensive two-dimensional chromatography.

nodes.lbl: retention volume of an unretained compound

comments: Ignoring any extra-column volume, \(V_{0}\) is equal to the interparticle volume of the column.

The retention volume of an unretained compound is related to the retention time of an unretained compound (in size-exclusion chromatography) and the flow rate (\(F_{\rm{c}}\)) by \(V_{0} = t_{0} \times F_{\rm{c}}\)
These molecules will be eluted first from the column.

basicPropertyValues.val: Retention volume of a sample component the molecules of which are larger than the largest pores of the particles of the stationary phase.

comments: The corresponding retention time is related to the retention time (in size-exclusion chromatography) (\(t_{\rm{R}}\)) and the flow rate (\(F_{\rm{c}}\)) by \(V_{\rm{R}} = t_{\rm{R}} \times F_{\rm{c}}\).

basicPropertyValues.val: Retention volume of a sample component, the molecules of which are smaller than the largest pores of the particles of the stationary phase but larger than the smallest pores.

comments: The total mobile phase volume is related to the total mobile phase time (in size-exclusion chromatography) (\(t_{\rm{t}}\)) and the flow rate (\(F_{\rm{c}}\)) by \(V_{\rm{t}} = t_{\rm{t}} \times F_{\rm{c}}\).

basicPropertyValues.val: Retention volume of a sample component, the molecules of which are smaller than the smallest pores of the particles of the stationary phase.

comments: For particles with relative molar mass greater than the exclusion limit the separation effect of the size-exclusion chromatography vanishes.

basicPropertyValues.val: Maximum value of the relative molecular masses of components in a specific polymer solvent system that can enter into the pores of the porous non-adsorbing material used in size-exclusion chromatography.

comments: In some areas, the symbol \(R_{\rm{s}}\) is used for the specific resolution. Due to the possibility of confusing it with the general resolution term (see peak resolution), the symbol \(R_{\rm{sp}}\) is suggested here.

The test compounds used for the determination of the specific resolution should have a narrow molecular-mass distribution (the ratio of the mass-average and number-average molecular masses should be equal to or less than about \(\pu{1.1}\)) and differ by a factor of about \(\pu{10}\) in their molar masses.

basicPropertyValues.val: Peak resolution also considering the molar masses (\(M_{1}\), \(M_{2}\)) of the two test compounds: \[R_{\rm{sp}} = \left[\frac{V_{\rm{R1}} - V_{\rm{R2}}}{(w_{\rm{b1}} + w_{\rm{b2}})/2} \right] \cdot \left[ \frac{1}{\log (M_{2}/M_{1})} \right]\]

Flavans are compounds with a 2-phenyl-3,4-dihydro-2\(H\)-1-benzopyran skeleton (1 in flavonoids), that may be substituted, and include flavan-3-ols (compounds derived from 2-phenyl-3,4-dihydro-2\(H\)-1-benzopyran-3-ol skeleton 2) and flavan-4-ones (compounds derived from 2-phenyl-2,3-dihydro-4\(H\)-1-benzopyran-4-one skeleton 3), which are generically designated as flavanols and flavanones, respectively. Compounds derived from 2-phenyl-3,4-dihydro-2\(H\)-1-benzopyran-3,4-diol skeleton 4 are flavan-3,4-diols, designated leukoanthocyanidins because these colourless compounds have their structure derived from that of an anthocyanidin, specifically they are dehydronated 3,4-dihydroxy-1,2,3,4-tetrahydroanthocyanidins.

comments: The term "flavonol" is used as a class name for compounds with a 3-hydroxy-2-phenyl-4\(H\)-1-benzopyran-4-one (3-hydroxy-2-phenyl-4\(H\)-chromen-4-one) skeleton 6.

basicPropertyValues.val: Flavones and 3-hydroxyflavones (flavonols) are compounds with a 2-phenyl-4\(H\)-1-benzopyran-4-one (2-phenyl-4\(H\)-chromen-4-one) skeleton 5.
Isoflavans are compounds with a 3-phenyl-3,4-dihydro-2\(H\)-1-benzopyran skeleton (see isoflavonoids). They may be substituted.
Isoflavones are compounds with a 3-phenyl-4$H$-1-benzopyran-4-one (3-phenyl-4$H$-chromen-4-one) skeleton 9. They may be substituted.
Neoflavans are compounds with a 4-phenyl-3,4-dihydro-2$H$-1-benzopyran skeleton (see neoflavonoids). They may be substituted.
Neoflavones are compounds with a 4-phenyl-2$H$-1-benzopyran-2-one (4-phenyl-2$H$-chromen-2-one) skeleton 11. They may be substituted.
Aurones are compounds derived from (2$Z$)-2-benzylidene-1-benzofuran-3(2$H$)-one [alternative name: (2$Z$)-2-(phenylmethylidene)-1-benzofuran-3(2$H$)-one] (aurone, compound 14).

Pterocarpans are compounds derived from (6a$R$,11a$R$)-6a,11a-dihydro-6$H$-[1]benzofuro[3,2-$c$][1]benzopyran (15), and their 6a,11a-didehydro derivatives 16 are named coumestans. They are numbered systematically following the numbering rules for fused ring systems.
Flavonolignans have structures based on flavonoids condensed with \(\ce{C6{-}C3}\) lignan precursors.
Biflavonoid and other flavonoid oligomers, which occur widely in nature, are exemplified and named in this recommendation (Flv-3.8).

comments: "Nominal property" is sometimes termed "nameable property", but not here.

The concept "nominal property" is defined as the opposite of "quantity", i.e. the former concept lacks the essential characteristic of "size" (or "magnitude"). In such cases, ISO 704:2009-6.5.4 allows a "negative definition".
The term "attribute" has sometimes been used to designate "nominal property", but not here.
The term "qualitative property" is also used, but not here as it is ambiguous because "ordinal quantity" is often included under that term.

basicPropertyValues.val: Property of a phenomenon, body, or substance, where the property has no size.

comments: "Kind-of-nominal-property" is sometimes termed "attribute", but not here.

basicPropertyValues.val: Defining aspect, common to mutually comparable nominal properties.
Kind-of-nominal-property indicating a class among nominal properties ordered according to nominal property values of a specified nominal property value set without relation to size.

comments: Taxonomy is the science of classification and its applications, usually regarding organisms.

basicPropertyValues.val: Category indicating a class of organisms within a recognized hierarchically structured nominal property value set.

comments: A dedicated kind-of-nominal-property is not specified to any individual person, in contrast to an individual nominal property, and it cannot have a nominal property value.

In clinical laboratory report forms, dedicated kind-of-nominal-properties may be described according to an internationally recommended NPU syntax from IFCC-IUPAC. The syntax is System(specification)-Component(specification); kind-of-property(specification). The last "specification" might contain information on the examination procedure or the nominal property value set. The initial capital for System and for Component is mandatory.Examples of the NPU syntax:.Blood—Plasma; colour({milky, red, yellow});.Erythrocytes(Blood)—Erythrocyte antigen; blood group({A, B, AB, O}).For examples 1-4 above, individual nominal properties can be written as follows (omitting patient identity and time but including the nominal property value for clarity):Patient—Spinal fluid; colour(visual)=reddish;DNA(Leukocytes)—CYP2D6 gene; sequence variation(allele specific PCR)=*1/*3;Expectoration—Bacterium; taxon(Phadebact coagglutination test)=Mycobacterium tuberculosis;Monocytes(Blood)—Nuclei; shape=oval.
The dedicated kinds-of-nominal-property examples above correspond to examples 1-4 of kind-of-nominal-property.
The patient"s name (or other identifier), location, and date and time of obtaining the sample of the system under consideration shall always be given in the clinical laboratory report.

basicPropertyValues.val: Kind-of-nominal-property with a sort of system and any pertinent sort(s) of component(s).

comments: The activity of examination essentially consists in comparing the property considered, i.e. the examinand by way of an examining system, with the property of a "reference" of similar nature. Such a reference may be personal and subjective, such as a person"s memory of a colour, or the reference may be objective, such as a nominal reference material.
The outcome of an examination is an examination result.

basicPropertyValues.val: Process of experimentally obtaining one or more nominal property values that can reasonably be attributed to a nominal property.

comments: The examined value may be obtained indirectly through examinations of other nominal properties, giving the examined value by using an algorithm which may involve measurement results and examination results.
The nominal property value of an examinand may be different from that of the property actually being examined due to changes of the system bearing the property during the examination.

basicPropertyValues.val: Nominal property intended to be examined.

comments: A human eye may be an essential element of an examining system.

basicPropertyValues.val: Set of one or more devices, including any reagent and supply, assembled and adapted to give information used to generate examined values from a nominal property value set.

comments: A quantity might also influence a nominal property.

basicPropertyValues.val: Nominal property that, in an examination, does not affect the nominal property that is actually examined, but affects the relation between the nominal indication on the examining system and the examination result.

comments: The phenomenon can be of a physical, chemical, or biological nature.

basicPropertyValues.val: Phenomenon serving as a basis of an examination.

comments: The laconic description in an examination method is insufficient to allow an examination with prescribed examination uncertainty, but aids in formulating one or more examination procedures.

basicPropertyValues.val: Generic description of a logical organization of operations used in an examination.

comments: An examination procedure can include a statement concerning a target examination uncertainty.

An examination procedure specifies the dedicated kind-of-nominal-property involved, any sampling, examining system, nominal reference material(s) needed, and the nominal property value set used. The examination procedure also specifies how many examined values that are necessary to obtain an examination result and how to estimate the expected examination uncertainty.
The information presented in an examination procedure is intended to be operational and should be sufficient for a trained operator to perform an examination satisfactorily.

basicPropertyValues.val: Detailed description of an examination according to one or more examination principles and to a given examination method and any decision algorithm necessary to obtain an examination result.
Nominal property value provided by an examining system.

comments: A blank nominal indication is necessary for quality assessment in some examination procedures.
A blank nominal indication shall not be confused with a quantity value below a detection limit.
A blank nominal indication, when the examination procedure is expected to produce a nominal property value, is an erroneous nominal property value.
The concept is often termed "negative control", but not here.

basicPropertyValues.val: Nominal indication obtained from an object similar to the one under investigation, except that the nominal property of interest is supposed not to be present, or is not contributing to the nominal indication.

Condition of examination out of a set of conditions that includes the same examination procedure, same operators, same examining system, same operating conditions, same location, and replicate examinations on the same or similar objects over a short period of time.

Condition of examination out of a set of conditions that includes the same examination procedure, same location, and replicate examinations on the same or similar objects over an extended period of time, but may include other conditions involving changes.

comments: The different examining systems may use different examination procedures.

basicPropertyValues.val: Condition of examination out of a set of conditions that includes different locations, operators, examining systems, and replicate examinations on the same or similar objects.

comments: A nominal property value can consist of a set of items.Example: The colours of the national flag of Switzerland are red and white.
Nominal property values can be words, alphanumerical codes, symbols, etc, but cannot enter into algebraic equations and is not related to a quantity dimension or a measurement unit.

The term "nominal quantity value" and its short form "nominal value" are used to indicate a concept concerning rounded or approximate quantity values. The term "nominal indication interval" is used to indicate a concept concerning rounded or approximate extreme indications.

basicPropertyValues.val: Feature common to equivalent individual nominal properties.

comments: A "nominal property value set" can be ordered by convention, for example in alphabetic order of words, or alphanumerical codes identifying nominal property values, or an order reflecting a classification, but neither of these is an ordering by size.

basicPropertyValues.val: Set of possible nominal property values for nominal properties of a given kind-of-nominal-property.

comments: A reference nominal property value can be a true nominal property value of an examinand, in which case it is unknown, or a conventional nominal property value, in which case it is known.

basicPropertyValues.val: Nominal property value used as a basis for comparison with nominal property values of nominal properties of the same kind-of-nominal-property.

comments: "Examination result" should not be confused with nominal property value set.

An "examination result" may be expressed as a single examined value and an examination uncertainty. If there is no dispersion of nominal property values attributed to the examinand or if the examination uncertainty is considered to be negligible for a specified purpose, the examination result may be expressed as a single examined value.
An "examination result" sometimes contains "relevant information" about the set of nominal property values, such that some may be more representative of the examinand than others.

basicPropertyValues.val: Set of nominal property values being attributed to an examinand together with any other available relevant information.

comments: The term "observed value" is sometimes used for "examined value", but not here.

basicPropertyValues.val: Nominal property value representing an examination result.
Nominal property value consistent with the definition of a nominal property.
Nominal property value attributed by agreement to a nominal property for a given purpose.

comments: Each examined value is either equivalent, or non-equivalent, to the reference nominal property value.
The examination trueness, in contrast to measurement trueness, is a quantity, and is complementary to examination uncertainty.

basicPropertyValues.val: Fraction of examined values identical to one or more reference nominal property values among all the examined values provided.

comments: Examination uncertainty is a part of an examination result.
Examination uncertainty is a quantity that is complementary to examination trueness.

With exception of the situation where the examination uncertainty is zero, some examined values differ from the reference nominal property value. In a comment to the examination result, the laboratory can provide information about other possible nominal property values, based on the information available.

basicPropertyValues.val: Fraction of examined values that is different from a reference nominal property value among all the examined values provided.

comments: An examination error is either present or absent.
Examination error is associated with an examined value, but not with an examining system.
Examination error should not be confused with production error or mistake.

basicPropertyValues.val: Disagreement between an examined value and a reference nominal property value.

comments: Examination accuracy is a feature of an individual examined value, but not of an examining system.

basicPropertyValues.val: Closeness of agreement between an examined value and a true nominal property value of an examinand.

comments: "Specified examination conditions" can, for example, be repeatability condition of examination, intermediate precision condition of examination, or reproducibility condition of examination.
A proportion distribution of a set of examined values describes proportions of data belonging to every possible nominal property value.

Examination precision can be expressed numerically by measures of dispersion of examined values such as Index of Qualitative Variation (IQV) and the Shannon"s entropy, under specified examination conditions. IQV varies between 0 (no dispersion, all examined values in a single class) and 1 (two or more classes with identical frequency). Shannon"s entropy varies between 0 (no dispersion, that is all examined values belong to a single category) and a maximum value equal to the logarithm (on basis 2) of the number of all categories. See Example.
Examination precision is a feature of an examining system used with a specified examination procedure.
Examination precision is used to define examination repeatability, intermediate examination precision, and examination reproducibility.

basicPropertyValues.val: Closeness of agreement between nominal indications on an examining system or examined values obtained by replicate examinations on the same or similar objects under specified examination conditions.

comments: Examination repeatability is a feature of an examining system used with a specified examination procedure.
Examination repeatability is a quantity.

basicPropertyValues.val: Examination precision under repeatability condition of examination.

comments: Intermediate examination precision is a feature of an examining system used with a specified examination procedure.
Intermediate examination precision is a quantity.

basicPropertyValues.val: Examination precision under intermediate precision condition of examination.

comments: Examination reproducibility is a feature of a set of examined values.
Examination reproducibility is a quantity.

basicPropertyValues.val: Examination precision under reproducibility condition of examination.

comments: Systematic examination error is a feature of an examining system used with a specified examination procedure.
Systematic examination errors for examined values are quantities.
The systematic examination error for examined values can be expressed for a set of examined values as examination bias.

basicPropertyValues.val: Fraction of examined values with examination error that in replicate examinations remains constant or varies in a predictable manner.

comments: Examination bias is a quantity.

If the proportion distributions of the reference nominal property values and the examined values are the same, there is no examination bias for the examining system. If the distributions differ there is an examination bias.
In some publications on analytical chemistry, "examination bias" is termed "lack of reliability", but this is not recommended here.

basicPropertyValues.val: Estimate of a systematic examination error.

comments: Target examination uncertainty is a quantity.

basicPropertyValues.val: Examination uncertainty specified as an acceptable fraction and decided on the basis of the intended use of examination results.
Subset of the nominal property value set containing the true nominal property value(s) of an examinand with a stated probability, based on the information available.
Probability that the set of true nominal property values of an examinand is contained within a specified nominal property value coverage set.

comments: The ISO Technical report (TR 79:2015) characterizes reference materials for "qualitative properties".

basicPropertyValues.val: Property of an examination result whereby it can be related to a reference through a documented unbroken chain of examination calibrations, each contributing to the examination uncertainty.
Comparability of examination results, for nominal properties of a given kind-of-nominal-property, that are examined and traceable to the same reference.

comments: The definition of this concept is not analogous to that of "metrological compatibility of measurement results" in the VIM.
Two compatible examination results can be identical.

basicPropertyValues.val: Property of a set of examination results for a specified examinand of a given kind-of-nominal-property that have overlapping nominal property value sets.

comments: A "realization of the definition of a given nominal property" can be provided by an examining system or a nominal reference material.

basicPropertyValues.val: Realization of the definition of a given nominal property (2.1), with stated nominal property value (3.1) and associated examination uncertainty (3.9), used as a reference.

comments: Nominal reference materials with or without assigned reference nominal property values can be used for control of examination precision, whereas only nominal reference materials with assigned reference nominal property values can be used for the control of examination calibration or evaluation of examination trueness.

basicPropertyValues.val: Material, sufficiently homogeneous and stable with reference to a specified nominal property, that has been established to be fit for its intended use in an examination.

comments: Examination calibration differs from that of calibration in the VIM, because in examination calibration there is no explicit mention of "nominal indication" and "examination uncertainty".

basicPropertyValues.val: Process that confers to one or more persons or to a device the capacity to provide nominal property values from specified examinations after having examined one or more examination standards.

Examination procedure accepted as providing examination results fit for their intended use in assessing examination trueness of examined values) obtained from other examination procedures for nominal properties of the same kind-of-nominal-property, in examination calibration, or in characterizing nominal reference materials.
Reference examination procedure used to obtain an examination result without relation to an examination standard for a nominal property of the same kind-of-nominal-property.
Examination standard recognized by signatories to an international agreement and intended to serve worldwide.

Examination standard recognized by national authority to serve in a state or economy as the basis for assigning nominal property values to other examination standards for the same kind-of-nominal-property.
Examination standard established using a primary reference examination procedure, or created as an artefact, chosen by convention.
Examination standard established through examination calibration with respect to a primary examination standard for a nominal property of the same kind-of-nominal-property.

Examination standard designated for the examination calibration of other examination standards for nominal properties of a given kind-of-nominal-property in a given organization or at a given location.

comments: A working examination standard is usually calibrated with respect to a reference examination standard.

basicPropertyValues.val: Examination standard that is used routinely to calibrate or verify examining systems.
Examination standard, sometimes of special construction, intended for transport between different locations.

comments: Sometimes, examination standards are used as transfer examination devices.

basicPropertyValues.val: Device used as an intermediary to compare examination standards.

comments: A nominal property value of an intrinsic examination standard is assigned by consensus and does not need to be established by relating it to another examination standard of the same type.

basicPropertyValues.val: Examination standard based on a reproducible nominal property of a phenomenon or substance.

comments: Conservation of an examination standard commonly includes periodic verification of predefined nominal properties or examination calibration, storage under suitable conditions, and specified care in use.

basicPropertyValues.val: Set of operations necessary to preserve the examinational properties of an examination standard within stated limits.
Examination standard used in examination calibration.

Nominal reference material accompanied by documentation issued by an authoritative body and providing one or more specified nominal property values with examination uncertainty and examination traceability, using valid examination procedures.
Linear velocity of the mobile phase across the average cross-section of the column.
Total retention time (\(t_{\rm{R}}\)) minus hold-up time (\(t_{\rm{M}}\)). \(t_{\rm{R}}^{\prime} = t_{\rm{R}} - t_{\rm{M}}\)

comments: The hold-up time includes any time that the component spends in the sample injector, the detector, and connectors.
The hold-up time is related to the hold-up volume (\(V_{\rm{M}}\)) and flow rate (\(F_{\rm{c}}\)) by \(t_{\rm{M}} = V_{\rm{M}}⁄F_{\rm{c}}\) .

basicPropertyValues.val: Time required to elute a component which is not retained by the stationary phase.

comments: The total retention time is related to the total retention volume (\(V_{\rm{R}}\)) and flow rate (\(F_{\rm{c}}\)) by \(t_{\rm{R}} = V_{\rm{R}}⁄F_{\rm{c}}\) .
Total retention time includes the hold-up time.

basicPropertyValues.val: Time between sample injection and the emergence of the peak maximum of the sample component of interest.

nodes.lbl: retention time of an unretained compound

comments: The retention time of an unretained compound is related to the retention volume of an unretained compound (in size-exclusion chromatography) and the flow rate (\(F_{\rm{c}}\)) by \(t_{0} = V_{0}/F_{\rm{c}}\)
This component will be eluted first from the column.

basicPropertyValues.val: Retention time of a sample component the molecules of which are larger than the largest pores of the particles of the stationary phase.
Measured or observed quantity in an experimental design.

comments: If the mean of autocorrelated data is estimated the standard deviation of the mean depends on sampling mode.

basicPropertyValues.val: Correlation of a variable with itself over a successive time or space intervals (lags).

comments: Data in a contingency table are categorical.

basicPropertyValues.val: Data, values of which are one of a fixed number of nominal categories.

comments: The entries in the cells of a contingency table can be frequency counts or relative frequencies.

basicPropertyValues.val: Type of table in a matrix format that displays the multivariate frequency distribution of variables.

comments: By convention a matrix is arranged with \(m\) rows and \(n\) columns.
For multi-way data the data is arranged in a hypercube of \(m \times n_{1} \times n_{2} \times\) …, where \(n_{1}\), \(n_{2}\) … are the kinds of explanatory variable.
Objects are also called "samples", but confusion with physical "test samples" in analytical chemistry should be avoided.
Variables are also called features, or explanatory variables.

basicPropertyValues.val: Measurement results on a system arranged in a \(m \times n\) matrix, with \(m\) objects and \(n\) variables.

comments: All data pre-processing methods imply some assumptions about the nature of the variability in the data set. It is important that these assumptions are understood and appropriate for the data set involved.

Aside from the three main categories of data pre-processing methods (mean centering, scaling and transformation), data pre-processing can refer to any other procedures carried out on the raw data, including mass binning and peak selection. In the case of multivariate images, this can also include region-of-interest selection and image filtering or binning.
More than one data pre-processing method can be applied to the same data set. The order of data pre-processing is important and can affect assumptions made on the nature of variance in the data set.
The term "pre-processing" is preferred to the term "pre-treatment" to reduce confusion with physical sample preparation or treatment prior to experimental analysis.

basicPropertyValues.val: Manipulation of raw data prior to a specified data analysis treatment.

comments: The method is used in chromatography to align peaks by their retention times.

basicPropertyValues.val: Process of synchronizing a data matrix so that it represents the same time shifts.

comments: "Test data" is also used for data from an unknown sample, and should not be used for "evaluation data".
Evaluation data should be independent of the data used to calibrate or train a model.

basicPropertyValues.val: Data used to validate a model.
Variable that influences the value of a response variable, and is used to build models of the response variable.

comments: Exploratory data analysis is recommended before deciding an approach to chemometric modelling.

basicPropertyValues.val: Summary of the main characteristics of data, often using graphical methods.

comments: Mean centering emphasises the differences between samples rather than differences between the samples and the variable’s origin (zero).
Mean centering is generally applied with other data pre-processing methods.

Mean centering is generally recommended for principal component analysis, partial least squares and discriminant analysis of data, where relative values across the samples are more important than their absolute deviation from zero. Mean centering is not compatible with non-negativity constraints in, for example, multivariate curve resolution.

basicPropertyValues.val: Data pre-processing in which the mean value of a variable is subtracted from data across all objects. \[a_{i,j}^{\ast} = a_{i,j} - \frac{1}{n} \sum \limits_{i\,=\,1}^{n} a_{i,j}\]

comments: MSC is typically used in near-infrared spectrometry to remove effects of non-homogeneous particle size.

basicPropertyValues.val: Data pre-processing in which a constant and a multiple of a reference data set is subtracted from data.

comments: The measurements results are often of the same kind of quantity.

basicPropertyValues.val: Data having two or more variables per object.

comments: For two groups of explanatory variables the data is termed ‘three-way’.
Models that decompose multi-way data include PARAFAC, Tucker3 model.

basicPropertyValues.val: Multivariate data having two or more kinds of explanatory variable per object.

comments: The population defines the kind of quantity of the location. For example, in a time series, the quantity giving the location is time, in QSAR the location is a point in design space.

basicPropertyValues.val: Sampling in which the sample locations are selected randomly from the whole population.

comments: Raw data can be an indication obtained from a measuring instrument or measuring system

basicPropertyValues.val: Data not yet subjected to analysis.

comments: A number of sampling units may be gathered together, for example in a package or box.
Examples of physical boundaries are capsules, containers, and bottles.

basicPropertyValues.val: Defined quantity of material having a boundary which may be physical or temporal.
Element-wise division of a data matrix by a scaling matrix.
Transformation using an approximating function to capture important patterns in data, while removing noise or other fine-scale structures.

comments: In a time series, the quantity giving the location is time.
The starting point may be assigned randomly within the first stratum.

basicPropertyValues.val: Sampling in which individual samples are taken at equal intervals in location.
Happenstance data that must be processed, or not processed, as is.

comments: A variable occupies a column of the data matrix.
Variance scaling equalizes the importance of each variable in multivariate data.
When used with mean centering variance scaling is known as autoscaling.

basicPropertyValues.val: Scaling in which the scaling matrix is the standard deviation of each variable across the objects. \[a_{i,j}^{\ast} = \frac{a_{i,j}}{s_{j}}\]
List of combinations of effects that are aliased (confounded).

comments: In a two-level design, the product of the coded levels for the aliased effects are equal.

basicPropertyValues.val: In a fractional-factorial design, effects for which the information obtained are identical.
Matrix of runs by factor levels in which each level is denoted by a code that represents the relative magnitude of the level.
Coefficient of a term in a response model.
Matrix with rows representing individual experimental treatments (possibly transformed according to the assumed model) which can be extended by deduced levels of other functions of factor levels.
Factor that is known to have no effect on the response, used in an experimental design, to estimate repeatability standard deviation.

comments: An "experimental design" (noun) usually refers to a table giving the levels of each factor for each run.

Experimental design is applied to determine the set of conditions that are required to obtain a product or process with desirable, often optimal properties. A characteristic of experimental design is that these conditions are determined in a statistically-optimal way.
Response surface methodology is considered an important part of experimental design.

basicPropertyValues.val: Efficient procedure for planning combinations of values of factors in experiments so that the data obtained can be analyzed to yield valid and objective conclusions.

comments: A design may be designated by the number of levels chosen for each factor, as in "two-level design".
When writing an experimental design the levels are usually coded.

basicPropertyValues.val: Value of a factor in an experimental design.

comments: A design, having \(L^{k}\) (see full-factorial design) experiments, is fractionated to \(L^{k - p}\) experiments where \(p\) is an integer \(\lt k\).
A fractional-factorial design is incomplete, but all incomplete designs are not fractional factorial.

The aim of a fractional design is to reduce the number of experiments by confounding low-order effects (e.g. main effect, two-way interaction) with high order interactions, which are assumed to be small.
The choice of design is governed by an alias structure.

basicPropertyValues.val: Experimental design obtained from a full-factorial design in which experiments are systematically removed to fulfill stated statistical requirements.

comments: If there are \(k\) factors, each at \(L\) levels, a full-factorial design has \(L^{k}\) runs.

basicPropertyValues.val: Experimental design with all possible combinations of factor levels.
Effect of a factor where the term is the product of two or more factors.
Effect of a factor where the term is a single factor.

comments: The model can be based on knowledge of the chemistry or physics of the system, but usually the model is empirical, being linear or quadratic with interaction terms.
To obtain information about the significance of effects, data is usually mean centered and assessed against a coded experimental design.

basicPropertyValues.val: Equation describing the response as a function of values of the factors.
Effect of a factor where the term is a factor raised to the power \(n\).
Minimization or maximization of a real function by systematically choosing the values of real or integer variables from within an allowed set.

comments: For \(4 \times N\) experiments, \(4 \times N − 1\) main effects and the mean are estimated.
If less than \(4 \times N − 1\) factors are being studied, dummy factors are inserted which allow estimation of the repeatability standard deviation of the measurement results.
Plackett–Burman designs are typically given for two levels, with a number of experiments that is a multiple of 4 but not a power of 2. (The latter case is a fractional-factorial design).

basicPropertyValues.val: Incomplete experimental design to estimate main effects for which each combination of factor levels for any pair of factors appears the same number of times.

comments: Full-factorial designs have no effects that are aliased and therefore have infinite resolution.
Resolution is used to describe the extent to which fractional-factorial designs create aliased effects.
The resolution is written as a Roman numeral.

basicPropertyValues.val: One more than the smallest nth-order interaction effect that some main effect is aliased with.

comments: Response surface methodology is usually associated with optimization. The model used is typically a quadratic function leading to a maximum or minimum response in the factor space.

The term "surface" implies two factors and a single response, when a plot of the modelled response as a function of values of the factors leads to a surface in the three-dimensional space. This can be generalized to any number of factors.

basicPropertyValues.val: Experimental design in which the response is modelled in terms of one or more factor levels.

comments: ALS is used to decompose multiple spectra (\(\boldsymbol{X}\)) into concentration (\(\boldsymbol{C}\)) and component spectra (\(\boldsymbol{S}\)). \(\boldsymbol{X} = \boldsymbol{C}\boldsymbol{S}^{\rm{T}}\). Because spectra and concentrations cannot be negative at each iteration negative values are set to zero.

basicPropertyValues.val: Solution to the multivariate decomposition of a data matrix in which iteratively a solution of one output matrix is used to compute the second matrix, after the application of constraints.

comments: A process called AR(1) is a first order process, meaning that the current value is based on the immediately preceding value. An AR(2) process has the current value based on the previous two values.

basicPropertyValues.val: Stochastic process in which future values are estimated based on a weighted sum of past values.

comments: Points in the scores plot (objects) that fall on a loadings vector are considered to be characterised by the variable associated with the vector.
The plots are scaled to facilitate interpretation.

basicPropertyValues.val: Combination plot of a scores plot as points and loadings plot as vectors for common factors.

comments: Bootstrapping is an alternative to cross validation in model validation.
Multiple resamples of the original data allow calculation of the distribution of a parameter of interest, and therefore its standard error (see example).
Random sampling with replacement is used when the data are assumed to be from an independent and identically-distributed population.

basicPropertyValues.val: Estimation of parameters by multiple re-sampling from measured data to approximate its distribution.
Linear combinations of data with the greatest correlation.

comments: The combinations with the greatest correlation, denoted U1 and V1 are known as the "first canonical variables". The next canonical functions, U2 and V2 are then restricted so that they are uncorrelated with U1 and V1. Everything is scaled so that the variance equals 1.
The relationship between the canonical variables is known as the canonical function.

basicPropertyValues.val: Multivariate technique which finds linear combinations of two sets of data that are most highly correlated.

comments: The common factors are not unique. Typically factors are rotated so that the factors are more easily interpreted in terms of the original variables.

basicPropertyValues.val: Factor analysis in which latent variables are calculated that maximise the correlation with observed variables.

comments: An appropriate PARAFAC model is a model where the components primarily reflect low-rank, trilinear variation in the data.
The principle of the method is to assess the degree of superdiagonality of the model.

basicPropertyValues.val: Method to assess the appropriateness of a PARAFAC model.
Factor analysis applied to categorical data in which orthogonal factors are obtained from a contingency table.

comments: The changing rank is calculated by principal-component analysis on an increasing data matrix.
The ordering variable may be time.

basicPropertyValues.val: Factor analysis that follows the change or evolution of the rank of the data matrix as a function of an ordered variable.

comments: Factor analysis is equivalent to a rotation in data space where the factors form the new axes. This is not necessarily rotation that maintains orthogonality except in the case of PCA.
Factor analysis methods include common factor analysis (also called ‘factor analysis’), principal component analysis, and multivariate curve resolution.
Hence \(\boldsymbol{X} = \boldsymbol{TP}^{\rm{T}} + \boldsymbol{E}\), where \(\boldsymbol{E}\) is a residual matrix.
The number of factors selected in factor analysis is smaller than the rank of the data matrix.
The residual matrix contains data that are not described by the factor analysis model, and is usually assumed to contain noise.

basicPropertyValues.val: Matrix decomposition of a data matrix (\(\boldsymbol{X}\)) into the product of a scores matrix (\(\boldsymbol{T}\)) and the transpose of the loadings matrix (\(\boldsymbol{P}^{\rm{T}}\)).

comments: Because the perturbation of the model is larger than in leave-one-out cross validation, the prediction ability of the G-fold cross validation is less optimistic than obtained with leave-one-out cross validation.
Objects 1 to \(N/G\) are removed on the first iteration, then objects \(N/G + 1\) to \(2N/G\) after replacement of the first \(N/G\) objects, and so on.

basicPropertyValues.val: Cross validation of a data set of \(N\) objects in which \(N/G\) objects are removed at each iteration of the procedure.

comments: A distinction can be made between ‘hidden variable’, which is considered to be an actual variable that is buried in the effects of other variables and noise, and a ‘latent variable’ that is entirely hypothetical.
The factors obtain from common factor analysis are termed latent variables.

basicPropertyValues.val: Variable that is inferred through a mathematical model from other variables that are observed.

comments: "Loadings" (plural) refers to a column in the loadings matrix that relates to a particular factor. "loading" (singular) is the particular contribution of a variable in the original space to the factor.

In multivariate curve resolution the term "pure component spectrum" is interchangeable with the term "loading" and is therefore deprecated. The term, in spectroscopy, may be confused with the spectrum for a pure material.
In principal component analysis the loadings are also the cosine angles between the variables and a particular factor.
The loadings on a factor reflect the relationships between the variables on that factor.

basicPropertyValues.val: Projection of a factor onto the variables.

comments: Usually the loadings associated with the early factors (1, 2, 3) are plotted to reveal relationships among the variables.

basicPropertyValues.val: Plot of one loading against variable number, or two or three loadings against each other.
Principal-component analysis that incorporates information about measurement uncertainty to develop models that are optimal in a maximum likelihood sense.

comments: Mean squared error of prediction is the square of root mean squared error of prediction.

basicPropertyValues.val: In multivariate calibration the average of the squared deviation of estimated values from the values of evaluation data. For \(N\) evaluation data where \(c_{i}\) is an observed value and \(\hat c_{i}\) is the predicted value. \[E_{\rm{MSEP}} = \frac{\sum\limits_{i\,=\,1}^{i\,=\,N} (\hat c_{i}\,-\, c_{i})^2}{N}\]

comments: MCR factors are extracted by the iterative minimization of the residual matrix using an alternating least squares approach, while applying suitable constraints, such as non-negativity, to the loadings and scores. MCR can be performed on the data matrix with or without data pre-processing.
MCR factors are not unique but are dependent on initial estimates, the number of factors to be resolved, constraints applied and convergence criteria. MCR factors are not required to be orthogonal.

basicPropertyValues.val: Factor analysis for the decomposition of multicomponent data into a linear sum of chemically-meaningful components when little or no prior information about the composition is available.

comments: The algorithm is very fast if only a few principal components are required, because the covariance matrix is not computed.

Writing the model as \(\boldsymbol{X} = \boldsymbol{T}\boldsymbol{P}^{\rm{T}} + \boldsymbol{E}\), the first principal component is computed from a data matrix. The data explained by this PC are then subtracted from \(\boldsymbol{X}\) and the algorithm applied again to residual data. The procedure is repeated until sufficient principal components are obtained.

basicPropertyValues.val: Iterative decomposition of a data matrix to give principal components.

comments: An often applied criterion for the mapping error (\(E\)) is the relative squared error between the true distance \(d_{ij}\) and mapped distance \(\delta_{ij}\).
Several iterative optimization procedures can be applied to minimize \(E\), such as steepest descent.

basicPropertyValues.val: Projection of objects defined in a multivariate space onto two- or three-dimensional space so that the distances between objects are preserved as well as possible.

comments: A representation of PARAFAC is \(x_{ijk} = \sum\limits_{r\,=\,1}^R a_{ir}b_{jr}c_{kr} + e_{ijk}\), where \(x_{ijk}\) is \(i\),\(j\),\(k\)-th element of the data matrix, and \(a_{ir}\), \(b_{jr}\), \(c_{kr}\) are the components of the loadings matrices. \(e_{ijk}\) is the \(i\),\(j\),\(k\)-th element of residual matrix.
A schematic representation of the PARAFAC model is
PARAFAC is a special case of the Tucker3 model (see Tucker tri-linear analysis) where the core matrix is the identity matrix, and \(r = s = t = R\) .
The PARAFAC model is also known as Canonical Decomposition (CANDECOMP).

basicPropertyValues.val: Decomposition of a three-way data matrix into the sum of sets of two-way loadings matrices.

synonyms.val: sum of squared errors of prediction

basicPropertyValues.val: In multivariate calibration for a prediction set of \(N\) data where \(c_{i}\) is an observed value and \(\hat c_{i}\) is the predicted value. \[E_{\rm{PRESS}} = \sum\limits_{i\,=\,1}^{i\,=\,N} (\hat c_{i} - c_{i})^2\]

comments: This procedure removes collinearity from the multivariate data and ensures that the new predictor variables, which are PCA scores, are distributed normally.

basicPropertyValues.val: Discriminant analysis on a multivariate data set that has been subject to principal-component analysis.

comments: The factorization is written \(\boldsymbol{X} = \boldsymbol{T}\boldsymbol{P}^{\rm{T}} + \boldsymbol{E}\), where \(\boldsymbol{T}\) is the scores matrix, \(\boldsymbol{P}\) is the loadings matrix and \(\boldsymbol{E}\) is a residual matrix.
The factors are orthogonal and are known as principal-component factors.
The term "principal-component analysis" is preferred to the plural "principal-components analysis".

basicPropertyValues.val: Factor analysis in which factors are calculated that successively capture the greatest variance in the data set.

comments: ISO 18115 recommends the use of the term "PCA factor".
The successive factors explain reducing fractions of the variance of the data set, and are written PC1, PC2 …

basicPropertyValues.val: Orthogonal factors obtained in a principal-component analysis.

comments: For two objects defined by \(\boldsymbol{X}\) and \(\boldsymbol{Y}\) the manipulation orthogonal rotation/reflection matrix \(\boldsymbol{R}\) Procrustes analysis minimises: \(\parallel\! \boldsymbol{Y} - \boldsymbol{X}\boldsymbol{R}\parallel^{2}\) subject to \(\boldsymbol{R}^{\rm{T}} \boldsymbol{R} = \boldsymbol{R} \boldsymbol{R}^{\rm{T}} = 1\).

Ordinary, or classical, Procrustes analysis is when an object is compared to one other object, which may be a reference shape. Generalized Procrustes analysis compares three or more shapes to an optimally-determined mean shape.

basicPropertyValues.val: Comparison of shapes of multi-dimensional objects by a series of geometrical transformations to minimise the sum of squared distances between the transformed and target structures while maintaining the internal structure of the objects.

nodes.lbl: root mean square error of cross validation

basicPropertyValues.val: Root mean square error of prediction when the predicted data is obtained by cross validation.

nodes.lbl: root mean squared error of prediction

comments: For completely independent, normally distributed evaluation data, RMSEP is a measure of the bias of the calibration.
RMSEP is related to the prediction error sum of squares (PRESS) by \(E_{\rm{RMSEP}} = \sqrt \frac{E_{\rm{PRESS}}}{N}\) .
When prediction is by cross validation RMSEP may be termed root mean square error of cross validation.

synonyms.val: root mean squared error of estimation

basicPropertyValues.val: In multivariate calibration or classification for \(N\) evaluation data where \(c_{i}\) is an observed value and \(\hat c_{i}\) is the predicted value \[E_{\rm{RMSEP}} = \sqrt {\frac{\sum\limits_{i\,=\,1}^{i\,=\,N} (\hat c_{i}\,-\,c_{i})^2}{N}}\]

comments: A data matrix \(\boldsymbol{D} = \boldsymbol{C} \times \boldsymbol{P}^{\rm{T}} + \boldsymbol{E}\) where \(\boldsymbol{C}\) is a concentration matrix, \(\boldsymbol{P}\) pure spectra of mixture components and \(\boldsymbol{E}\) an error matrix. Pure spectra are estimated \(\boldsymbol{\hat Y}\) which allows projection of a concentration matrix \(\boldsymbol{C^{\ast}}\) from which the data matrix can be reconstructed and compared with the measured spectra. \[\left\{ {\matrix{ {\boldsymbol{\hat P} = \boldsymbol{D}^{\rm{T}} \boldsymbol{C}(\boldsymbol{C}^{\rm{T}}\boldsymbol{C})}^{-1} \cr {\boldsymbol{C^{*}} = \boldsymbol{C}\boldsymbol{\hat P}(\boldsymbol{\hat P}^{\rm{T}}\boldsymbol{\hat P})}^{-1} \cr}} \right. {\rm{then}}\;{\boldsymbol{D}_{{\rm{recon}}}} = \boldsymbol{C^{*}} \times \boldsymbol{\hat P}^{\rm{T}}\]
Second derivatives of spectra can be used for modelling.
The directly-measured variables are called "pure variables" in the method.

basicPropertyValues.val: Interactive method to obtain concentrations and pure spectra from spectra of mixtures using directly-measured variables.

comments: In principal-component analysis, the factors are orthogonal and the scores are an orthogonal projection of the objects onto a factor.
The scores on a factor reflect the relationships between objects for that factor.
The term scores (plural) refers to a whole column in the scores matrix that relates to a particular factor. The term score (singular) is the projection of a particular object onto the factor.

basicPropertyValues.val: Factor analysis projection of an object onto a factor.

comments: Usually the scores associated with the early factors (1, 2, 3) are plotted to reveal relationships among the objects.

basicPropertyValues.val: Plot of one score against object number, or two or three scores against each other.

comments: The function \(E(\rm{s})\) to be minimized is analogous to the internal energy of the system in that state. The goal is to bring the system, from an arbitrary initial state, to a state with the minimum possible energy. At each step, the heuristic considers some neighbouring state \(s^{\prime}\) of the current state \(s\), and probabilistically decides between moving the system to state \(s^{\prime}\) or staying in state \(s\). These probabilities ultimately lead the system to move to states of lower energy. Typically this step is repeated until the system reaches a state that is good enough for the application, or until a given computation budget has been exhausted.

basicPropertyValues.val: Generic probabilistic meta-heuristic to locate a good approximation to the global optimum of a given function in a large search space, in which there is a slow decrease in the probability of accepting worse solutions as the solution space is explored.

comments: If \(\boldsymbol{M}\) is a data matrix with \(m\) objects and \(n\) variables, the matrix \(\boldsymbol{U}\) is the scores matrix, the diagonal of \(\boldsymbol{\Sigma}\) contain the square roots of the eigenvalues and \(\boldsymbol{V}\) is the loadings matrix.

basicPropertyValues.val: A factorization of an \(m \times n\) matrix (\(\boldsymbol{M}\)) such that \(\boldsymbol{M} = \boldsymbol{U}\boldsymbol{\Sigma} \boldsymbol{V}^{T}\), where \(\boldsymbol{U}\) is an \(m \times m\) matrix, \(\boldsymbol{\Sigma}\) is a \(m \times n\) matrix and \(\boldsymbol{V}^{\rm{T}}\) is a \(n \times n\) matrix.

comments: A graphical representation of the Tucker3 model is

A representation of the Tucker3 model is \[x_{ijk} = \sum\limits_{r\,=\,1}^R \sum\limits_{s\,=\,1}^S \sum\limits_{t\,=\,1}^T a_{ir}b_{js}{c_{kt}z_{rst} + e_{ijk}}\] where \(x_{ijk}\) is the data matrix, \(a_{ir}\), \(b_{js}\), \(c_{kt}\) are the loadings matrices, and \(z_{rst}\) is the core matrix. \(e_{ijk}\) is the residual matrix.

basicPropertyValues.val: Decomposition of a three-way data matrix into a three-way core matrix, and three, two-way loadings matrices.

comments: Backward chaining is used in backward propagation to train an artificial neural network.

basicPropertyValues.val: Inference method from hypothesis to data that supports the hypothesis
Supervised classification method for an artificial neural network in which weights of connections between nodes are calculated from the known output layer back to the input layer.

comments: Interrelationships between variables that have not yet been selected are ignored, and variables already added, which may become largely redundant through subsequent additions, cannot be removed.
Significant loss is tested by an F-test

basicPropertyValues.val: Linear discriminant analysis in which variables to build the discriminant functions are removed one at a time to minimise the loss of discrimination, until there is a significant loss.

Distance (\(d_{i,j}\)) between two objects (\(i\) and \(j\)) calculated as the sum of the absolute difference between \(k\) variables (\(x\)) that describe the objects. \[d_{i,j} = \sum\limits_{k\,=\,1}^{k\,=\,N} \vert x_{i,k} - x_{j,k}\vert\]

comments: Complete linkage tends to find compact clusters of approximately equal size.

basicPropertyValues.val: Linkage criterion in hierarchical clustering in which the distance between two clusters is the distance between those two objects (one from each cluster) that are farthest apart.
