comments: The objects are successively grouped (or un-grouped) in each layer of the dendrogram, where the length of the linking lines is proportional to the dissimilarity of the objects.

basicPropertyValues.val: Tree diagram used to illustrate the arrangement of clusters produced by hierarchical clustering.

comments: Soft independent modelling of class analogy is an example of the use of disjoint principal component analysis.
When a PCA model is obtained using all classes, it is known as conjoint PCA.

basicPropertyValues.val: Principal-component analysis (PCA) independently performed on each class as a step in classification.

Distance (\(d_{i,j}\)) between two objects (\(i\) and \(j\)) calculated as the square root of the sum of the squared differences between \(k\) variables (\(x\)) that describe the objects. \[d_{i,j} = \sqrt {\sum\limits_{k\,=\,1}^{k\,=\,N} (x_{i,k} - x_{j,k})^2}\]

comments: In logic, forward chaining is the application of modus ponens (if \(\rm{P}\) implies \(\rm{Q}\), given \(\rm{P}\) then \(\rm{Q}\)).

basicPropertyValues.val: Inference method from data to hypothesis.

comments: Interrelationships between variables that have not yet been selected are ignored, and variables already added, which may become largely redundant through subsequent additions, cannot be removed.
Significant improvement is usually tested by an F-test

basicPropertyValues.val: Linear discriminant analysis in which variables to build the discriminant functions are introduced one at a time to maximise the discrimination, until there is no significant improvement.

comments: In so-called hard cluster algorithms membership of a group can only take values 0 or 1, but in fuzzy clustering any value between 0 and 1 is allowed subject to the sum of all memberships of an object being 1.

basicPropertyValues.val: Classification in which membership of an object in each possible class is given a weight between zero and one.
Group of nodes in an artificial neural network between input layer and output layer.

comments: Distance measures include Euclidean distance, Mahalanobis distance and city-block distance.
Linkage criteria include single linkage, complete linkage.

basicPropertyValues.val: Pattern recognition in which objects are linked together by use of an appropriate measure of distance between pairs of objects, and a linkage criterion, which specifies the dissimilarity of sets as a function of the pairwise distances between objects.

comments: Although \(k\)-means clustering is called unsupervised classification the value of \(k\) may be specified.

basicPropertyValues.val: Unsupervised classification method which partitions objects into \(k\) groups, in which each object belongs to the group with the nearest mean.

comments: An object is classified by a majority vote of its \(k\)-nearest neighbours, with the object being assigned to the class most common.
When \(k = 1\) the method is known as "nearest neighbour".
\(k\) is a small positive integer.

basicPropertyValues.val: Non-parametric supervised classification method for objects based on the closest training examples in the variable space.
Type of self-organising map with low dimensional grid.
Discriminant analysis in which the criterion function is based on the pooled covariance matrix.

Distance (\(d_{i,j}\)) between an object characterised by vector of variables \(\boldsymbol{x}_{i}\) and the centroid of a class \(\boldsymbol{\mu}_{j}\) with covariance matrix \(\boldsymbol{S}\) calculated as \[d_{i,j} = \sqrt {(\boldsymbol{x}_{i} - \boldsymbol{\mu}_{j})^T \boldsymbol{S}^{-1}(\boldsymbol{x}_{i} - \boldsymbol{\mu}_{j})}\] where \(\boldsymbol{S}\) is the covariance matrix of the variables.

comments: Misclassification rate is an estimate of the misclassification probability.
Misclassification rate may be calculated for an evaluation data set, or in leave-one-out cross validation.

basicPropertyValues.val: Fraction of objects incorrectly assigned to a group in supervised classification.

comments: The assignment of an object to a group may be in the form of a probability of membership.

basicPropertyValues.val: Classification identifying objects of a specific class amongst all objects, by learning from training data containing only objects of the specific class.

comments: Nodes are arranged in layers, input, hidden and output.
The value of a node is used in the calculation of nodes in subsequent layers.

basicPropertyValues.val: Locations in an artificial neural network that carry values that are calculated from values of connected nodes and weights by a transfer.

comments: PLS-DA can also be useful for exploratory data analysis.

PLS-DA results depend on data pre-processing and choice of parameters and so is believed to be more difficult to implement well than other forms of discriminant analysis such as linear discriminant analysis, quadratic discriminant analysis or regularized discriminant analysis.

basicPropertyValues.val: Linear classification in which the criterion function is obtained by partial least squares analysis.
Discriminant analysis in which the criterion function is based on the individual within-group covariance matrix.

comments: The covariance matrix (\(\sum_{k}(\lambda)\)) is related to the class covariance matrix (\(\sum_{k}\)) and the pooled covariance matrix (\(\sum_{\rm{pooled}}\)) by \(\sum_{k}(\lambda) = (1 - \lambda)\sum_{k} + \lambda\sum_{\rm{pooled}}\)

basicPropertyValues.val: Discriminant analysis in which the criterion function is based on a combination of pooled covariance matrix and the individual within-group covariance matrix.

comments: A similarity index may be in the interval, where 0 is complete dissimilarity and 1 is complete equivalence.
When the term "distance" is used the quantity is some function of the differences of coordinates in the multivariate data space.

basicPropertyValues.val: Quantity that describes the equivalence of two objects characterised by multivariate data.

comments: A drawback of this method is the so-called chaining phenomenon, which refers to the gradual growth of a cluster as one element at a time gets added to it. This may lead to impractically heterogeneous clusters and difficulties in defining classes that could usefully subdivide the data.

basicPropertyValues.val: Linkage criterion in hierarchical clustering in which the distance between two clusters is the distance between those two objects (one from each cluster) that are closest together.

nodes.lbl: soft independent modelling of class analogy

comments: SIMCA is an example of the use of disjoint principal component analysis.
The number of principal-component factors chosen for each class is determined by cross validation.

basicPropertyValues.val: Supervised classification that performs a principal-component analysis on each class, and then an unknown is assigned to the class with which it has the lowest residual variance.

comments: Algorithms for supervised classification include discriminant analysis, support vector machine, artificial neural network, Bayesian classifier.

basicPropertyValues.val: Classification in which, in a first step, a model is built using data from objects of known classes, and in a second step, the model is applied to new data to assign a class to unknown objects.

comments: The Tanimoto index is essentially similar to the Jaccard index. (See https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaccard_index).
The Tanimoto index is used in drug discovery and QSAR for comparison of structures in large data bases in an efficient way.
The rules for agreement must be defined. For example in an elemental analysis, element concentrations equivalent within \(\pu{20\%}\).

basicPropertyValues.val: Fraction of variables that are considered to agree between two objects.

comments: Algorithms for unsupervised classification include k-means cluster analysis, hierarchical cluster analysis.
The number of groups may be specified.

basicPropertyValues.val: Classification in which no prior information about membership of groups is known.

nodes.lbl: unweighted pair group method with arithmetic mean

basicPropertyValues.val: Linkage criterion in hierarchical clustering in which the distance between two clusters is the average of all distances between pairs of objects.

comments: The initial cluster distances in Ward’s minimum variance method are the squared Euclidean distance.

basicPropertyValues.val: Linkage criterion in hierarchical clustering in which the within-cluster variance is minimized.

comments: Least squares regression is used as a synonym for ordinary least squares regression. The full term should be used if there is ambiguity about the kind of regression being performed.

basicPropertyValues.val: Regression that minimizes the sum of squared differences between observed values of a variable and the values predicted by a model.

comments: The model for EIV regression is \[\left\{\matrix{c_{i} = \alpha + \beta x_{i}^{*} + \varepsilon_{i} \cr x_{i} = x_{i}^{*} + \eta_{i} \cr}\right.\] where \(x^{*}\) is the true value of the predictor variable, \(c_{i}\) concentration and \(\varepsilon\) and \(\eta\) are errors.
Total least squares regression is performed by singular value decomposition.
When the errors \(\varepsilon\) and \(\eta\) have the same variance the method is called orthogonal regression and minimises the perpendicular distance of a point to the regression line.

basicPropertyValues.val: Least squares regression in which both the response variable and predictor variable have measurement error.

comments: Mean squared error of calibration is the square of the root mean squared error of calibration.

basicPropertyValues.val: In calibration for \(N\) calibration data where \(c_{i}\) is an observed value and \(\hat c_{i}\) is the value predicted by the calibration function. \[E_{\rm{MSEC}} = \frac{\sum\limits_{i\,=\,1}^{i\,=\,N} (\hat c_{i} - c_{i})^2}{N}\]

comments: If \(\boldsymbol{X}^{\rm{T}} \boldsymbol{X}\) has full rank only because of noise, the solution can become unstable.

In \(\boldsymbol{X} \boldsymbol{b} = \boldsymbol{c} + \boldsymbol{e}\) (where \(\boldsymbol{X}\) is a vector of indications, \(\boldsymbol{b}\) are coefficients of the model, \(\boldsymbol{c}\) is a vector of values of the quantity of interest and \(\boldsymbol{e}\) a vector of errors), \(\boldsymbol{b} = \boldsymbol{X^{+}} \boldsymbol{c}\), where \(\boldsymbol{X^{+}}\) is the pseudo-inverse of \(\boldsymbol{X}\), calculated as \(\boldsymbol{X^{+}} = (\boldsymbol{X}^{\rm{T}} \boldsymbol{X})^{-1} \boldsymbol{X}^{\rm{T}}\)
It is assumed that \(\boldsymbol{X}^{\rm{T}} \boldsymbol{X}\) has full rank, i.e. there are more objects than variables, and the variables are independent.

basicPropertyValues.val: Multivariate calibration in which the coefficients of the regression are calculated directly from the indications and values of standards.

comments: In multivariate regression and calibration the problem is usually posed as a relation between the indications \(\boldsymbol{X}\) (which are multivariate) and the property to be measured \(\boldsymbol{y}\). Note that this is a reversal of the traditional form, \(x\) (concentration)/\(y\ (\rm{g})\) (indication) of linear calibration. \(\boldsymbol{X}\) is a vector of observations (indications), and \(\boldsymbol{c}\) a vector of concentrations. In matrix form: \(\boldsymbol{X} \boldsymbol{b} = \boldsymbol{c} + \boldsymbol{e}\) where \(\boldsymbol{b}\) are the coefficients of the model and \(\boldsymbol{e}\) is a vector of errors.

Regression establishes the coefficients \(\boldsymbol{b}\) (\(\boldsymbol{X} \boldsymbol{b} = \boldsymbol{c} + \boldsymbol{e}\)) from given indications \(\boldsymbol{X}\), or some factorization of \(\boldsymbol{X}\), and values \(\boldsymbol{c}\), or some factorization of \(\boldsymbol{c}\). Given indications \(\boldsymbol{X}_{\rm{u}}\) from an unknown sample, the quantity value \(c_{\rm{u}}\) can be calculated.

basicPropertyValues.val: Calibration in which the indications are multivariate data.

comments: Assumptions of the model are that error is only in the dependent variable, Normally-distributed, and homoscedastic.
OLSR is used for calibration and multivariate calibration.

basicPropertyValues.val: Least squares regression that minimizes the sum of squared differences between the known values of dependent variable and values predicted by a linear model.

comments: PLS finds factors (latent variables) in observed variables \(\boldsymbol{X}\) that explain the maximum variance in the variable(s) \(\boldsymbol{c}\), using the simultaneous decomposition of the two. It removes redundant information from the regression, i.e. factors describing large amounts of variance in the observed data that does not correlate with the predictions.
PLS may also be used in classification. See partial least squares discriminant analysis.

PLS1 refers to PLS for a single "c" variable. PLS2 is PLS that simultaneously obtains values for two or more "c" variables. Therefore in the equations of Note 2, PLS1 has vectors \(\boldsymbol{c}\) and \(\boldsymbol{q}\) and PLS2 has matrices \(\boldsymbol{C}\) and \(\boldsymbol{Q}\).

The decompositions are \(\boldsymbol{X} = \boldsymbol{T}_{k}\boldsymbol{P}_{k}^{\rm{T}} + \boldsymbol{E}\) and \(\boldsymbol{C} = \boldsymbol{U}_{k}\boldsymbol{Q}_{k}^{\rm{T}} + \boldsymbol{F}\), and \(\boldsymbol{X^{+}} = \boldsymbol{W}_{k} (\boldsymbol{P}_{k}\boldsymbol{W}_{k})^{-1} (\boldsymbol{T}_{k}^{\rm{T}}\boldsymbol{T}_{k})^{-1} \boldsymbol{T}_{k}^{\rm{T}}\), where \(\boldsymbol{W}\) are weights that maintain orthogonal scores.

When used for multivariate calibration, evaluation data or cross validation may be used to choose the number of PLS factors and assess the accuracy of the prediction (although the same data must not be used to do both). This is important to guard against overfitting.

basicPropertyValues.val: Multivariate calibration which finds factors that maximise covariance between two blocks of data.

comments: PCA decomposes the predictor variable data \(\boldsymbol{X}\) into \(k\) principal component factors \(\boldsymbol{\hat X}_{k} = \boldsymbol{T}_{k}\boldsymbol{P}_{k}^{\rm{T}}\), where \(k\) may be determined by cross validation. The dependent variable \(\boldsymbol{c}\) is then regressed against \(\boldsymbol{\hat X}_{k}\), \(\boldsymbol{c} = \boldsymbol{\hat X}_{k} \boldsymbol{\hat b}\).
The factorization gives orthogonal factors, but no information about the predicted variable \(\boldsymbol{c}\) is used.

basicPropertyValues.val: Multivariate calibration in which a dependent variable is regressed against the scores of a chosen number of factors obtained from principal-component analysis of the predictor variable.

nodes.lbl: root mean squared error of calibration

comments: Overfitting results in a small RMSEC, but poor predictive ability.

basicPropertyValues.val: In calibration for \(N\) calibration data where \(c_{i}\) is an observed value and \(\hat c_{i}\) is the value predicted by the calibration function. \[E_{\rm{RMSEC}} = \sqrt \frac{\sum\limits_{i\,=\,1}^{i,=\,N} (\hat c_{i} - c_{i})^2}{N}\]

comments: Underfitting generally occurs when a model is not sufficiently complex, such as having too few parameters.

basicPropertyValues.val: Condition in which a model fails to describe the data adequately.

comments: If the only source of dispersion in the dependent variable is normally distributed, the weights are the inverse of the variance of each value.
It is assumed the weights are known exactly.
The nonnegative constants are called weights.

basicPropertyValues.val: Least squares regression in which a nonnegative constant is associated with each value of the dependent variable.
Distance from the interface beyond which mass transfer is determined by convection.

comments: Defined amounts are usually given as a volume fraction of the sample volume (e.g. \(\pu{1\%}\), \(\pu{5\%}\) or \(\pu{10\%}\), etc.).
The breakthrough volume, \(V_{\rm{B}}\), for a particular compound and sampling device is determined by its breakthrough curve (see figure).

basicPropertyValues.val: Sample volume at which a defined amount of an analyte pumped continuously through an extraction device will begin to be eluted. Typical breakthrough curve indicating the breakthrough volume \(V_{\rm{B}}\) and the sample volume corresponding to the saturation capacity of the sorbent \(V_{\rm{C}}\) (\(V_{\rm{R}}\) corresponds to the chromatographic elution volume and \(\upsigma_{\rm{v}}\) the standard deviation of the derivative of the curve).Typical breakthrough curve indicating the breakthrough volume \(V_{\rm{B}}\) and the sample volume corresponding to the saturation capacity of the sorbent \(V_{\rm{C}}\) (\(V_{\rm{R}}\) corresponds to the chromatographic elution volume and \(\upsigma_{\rm{v}}\) the standard deviation of the derivative of the curve).

comments: Ion-pair extraction can also be done by adding the complementary-charge containing compound to the organic phase before extraction.

basicPropertyValues.val: Transfer of ions from an aqueous phase to an immiscible liquid (or solid) phase by adding an ion of complementary charge to the aqueous phase.

comments: If extraction occurs exclusively at the surface then adsorbent is the preferred term and if exclusively in the bulk then absorbent should be used.

Sorbent is typically used explicitly to describe a condensed phase where extraction occurs simultaneously by adsorption and absorption (termed sorption), or where the true mechanism has not been established and the use of adsorbent or absorbent would be inappropriate.

basicPropertyValues.val: Condensed phase where extraction of analytes can occur at the surface and in the bulk.

comments: In extractions employing a semipermeable membrane for phase separation the acceptor phase is the phase to which analytes are transferred from the donor phase.
When the acceptor phase is a liquid the term acceptor solution may be used.

basicPropertyValues.val: Component of a multi-phase system into which the target analytes are extracted.
Continuous extraction with movement of the sample matrix with respect to the extraction phase.

comments: Term "batch" is also used in extraction to indicate a number of samples extracted sequentially or simultaneously by the same procedure (e.g. extraction of sample batch(es)).

basicPropertyValues.val: Extraction in which the extraction phase and the sample are confined in an extraction vessel and processed according to a defined procedure.
Internal standard that is incorporated in the extraction phase for calibration.

comments: Activated charcoal was used in early applications, but a wider selection of carbon materials are currently used, with properties tailored to each application.

basicPropertyValues.val: Tube filled with charcoal typically used to adsorb analytes from the gas or liquid phase.
Extraction in which the sample is continuously introduced into the extraction device.

comments: The phases are either immiscible or separated by a membrane.

basicPropertyValues.val: Extraction in which both phases are continuously added (or changed) and flow (or move) in opposite directions as the extraction progresses.
In extraction, the sample or sample solution.

comments: The extraction phase can be a gas or a liquid.

basicPropertyValues.val: Extraction in which clean (or recycled) extraction phase is continuously passed through the sample.
Type of extraction where the intent is a complete extraction of the analytes.
Calibration employing a simplified sample matrix spiked with target analyte embodying a reference value of the measurand.
Liquid, solid, or gas phase in contact with the sample for the purpose of removal of analytes from the sample matrix.
Rate at which analytes are transferred from the sample to the extraction phase.

comments: If feed is used without qualification, the term may be taken to designate the initial liquid phase containing the main solute to be transferred or sample solution in a batch process.

basicPropertyValues.val: Solution or gas containing analyte introduced into an extraction.
Extraction in a biphasic system in which the main component of one phase is a highly fluorinated solvent (liquid-liquid extraction) or highly fluorinated sorbent (solid-phase extraction).
Dissolution of sample components from a solid with a liquid in which the solid phase is not wholly soluble.

comments: Matrix-matched calibration is used to minimize the matrix effect on the measurement of target measurands.

basicPropertyValues.val: Calibration employing external calibration in which standard solutions of target are prepared in a solution of analyte-free matrix.
Plate with multiple wells for individual samples.

comments: Many extractions are controlled by several parameters and their interactions. Optimum conditions are more efficiently identified by multivariate methods.

basicPropertyValues.val: Adjustment of extraction parameters to achieve a defined goal.
Extraction process driven by diffusion of analytes towards the extraction phase.
Addition of an electrolyte to an aqueous phase to decrease the distribution ratio of the analyte(s) or matrix.

comments: The most commonly used approaches in elemental analysis are the BCR (now termed Standards, Measurement and Testing Program) and Tessier procedures.

basicPropertyValues.val: Extraction wherein extractants of increasing strength or different chemical character are used in order to extract analytes of interest.

comments: If the analytes are initially present as a solution in an immiscible liquid phase the process is synonymous with liquid-liquid extraction.
If the sample is a solid that is partially soluble in the extraction phase then leaching may be a more appropriate term.

basicPropertyValues.val: Batch extraction in which the extraction phase attains a constant composition before phase separation.

comments: The term equilibrium should not be used to describe this situation.

basicPropertyValues.val: State of a continuous process operating in such a way that the concentration of solutes in exit streams remains constant with respect to time for constant feed concentrations, even though the two phases are not necessarily in thermodynamic equilibrium in any part of the process.
A passive sampling or active sampling strategy over a relatively long time, during which the amount of analyte(s) extracted is proportional to its average (mean) concentration over that time.
Type of chemical vapour generation wherein volatile hydrides are generated by reaction with (usually) borane complexes in aqueous solution.

comments: Closed-loop extraction was developed for trace analysis of volatile compounds (at mass concentrations of \(\pu{ng L-1}\)) in drinking water.

basicPropertyValues.val: Extraction by a fixed volume of gas continuously recycled through the sample and a sorbent trap by a pump in a closed-circuit arrangement.Typical apparatus for closed-loop stripping analysis.

comments: Typically, cryogenic traps have a low thermal mass to respond rapidly to changes in temperature and are prepared from short lengths of capillary tubing. Sub-ambient temperatures are required for the efficient collection of analytes from a flowing gas stream and above ambient temperatures for evaporation into a flowing gas stream for analysis, usually by gas chromatography or atomic spectrometry.

basicPropertyValues.val: Device used to concentrate volatile analytes from the gas phase by condensation on a cold surface.

comments: Both liquid and solid sorbents are used for trapping.
There are many design variations.

basicPropertyValues.val: Apparatus for the extraction of volatile analytes from a flowing gas stream by diffusion to the wall of a collection vessel, where they are retained by chemisorption or strong physisorption by the wall coating.

comments: A typical apparatus for purge-and-trap is shown in the figure below.

Purge-and-trap is a version of dynamic headspace analysis in which volatile compounds are purged from solution by a continuous stream of gas bubbles (sparging gas) and transported through the headspace to a sorbent or cryogenic trap for collection.

basicPropertyValues.val: Continuous removal of headspace above a sample by a flow of inert gas over or through the sample until all or a significant portion of the analytes have been removed from the sample. Sample vapours are typically transferred to a sorbent trap or cryogenic trap for collection.Typical apparatus for analysis by dynamic headspace (purge and trap). The gas flow (sparging gas) enters at the bottom of the sample container transporting volatile compounds through the headspace and purge head to the desorption tube for collection.

comments: If the separation solvent forms an azeotrope with one or more sample components the process is called azeotropic distillation.

basicPropertyValues.val: Separation of close-boiling liquids by fractional distillation in the presence of a low-volatility solvent or salt that selectively interacts with one or more components of the mixture, increasing the difference in vapour pressure of the sample components.
Thermal desorption where the temperature of a packed tube or cryogenic trap is rapidly increased to transfer condensed or sorbed compounds to the gas phase.

comments: Equilibrium between the condensed and vapor phases no longer exists. As a consequence, the possibility of matrix interferences is reduced and the fraction extracted for low-volatility compounds is increased.
The full-evaporation technique is used with both static headspace analysis and dynamic headspace analysis.

basicPropertyValues.val: Small volume of sample in a headspace vessel maintained at a temperature sufficient to cause complete evaporation of analytes.
Volume of gas phase above a sample in a closed container.

comments: At equilibrium the headspace is sampled and the remainder (or most of it) is exhausted and replaced by fresh gas phase. The process is repeated and the original sample concentration estimated from the peak areas for two consecutive extractions. \[A_{\rm{T}} = \frac{A_{1}^{2}}{A_{1} - A_{2}}\] where \(A_{\rm{T}}\) = estimated sum of all partial peak areas corresponding to exhaustive extraction, \(A_{1}\) the peak area obtained from the first headspace fraction, and \(A_{2}\) the peak area obtained in the second (consecutive) headspace fraction.
External calibration is required to convert peak areas into sample concentration.

basicPropertyValues.val: Dynamic gas extraction carried out stepwise, with sequential analysis of a number of headspace samples taken from the same vial.

comments: A typical apparatus for simultaneous steam distillation-solvent extraction with a lighter-than-water extraction solvent is shown in the figure below.

basicPropertyValues.val: Extraction in which a sample dispersed in water and a water immiscible organic solvent (extraction phase) in separate flasks are heated simultaneously and their vapours co-condensed and separated into two streams in which water is returned to the sample flask and the extraction phase to the organic solvent flask.Apparatus for simultaneous steam distillation-solvent extraction with a lighter-than-water extraction phase. A = aqueous sample solution or slurry; B = immiscible organic solvent and receiving flask for extracted compounds; C = bowl for phase separation; D, E, F, and G are solvent or vapour transfer arms; and H = entry port for additional solvent or alternative sample introduction position for continuous liquid–liquid extraction. Switching the position of flasks A and B allows extraction with a heavier-than-water extraction solvent.

comments: The performance of a sorbent tube depends on the sorbent type, temperature, gas flow rate, and desorption time.

basicPropertyValues.val: Tube filled with porous sorbent typically used to extract analytes from the gas phase.

comments: At equilibrium, the analyte concentration in the gas phase is related to the sample concentration by a partition constant.
The sample vessel is thermostatted.

basicPropertyValues.val: Method of analysis, in which a small aliquot of the gas phase in contact with the sample in a closed container is withdrawn for analysis.

comments: The volatile compounds are typically transported by a gas stream to a sorbent tube or cryogenic trap for collection.

basicPropertyValues.val: Release of volatile compounds from a sample by heat.

comments: Volatile compounds in the sample solution pass into the gas phase and are continuously swept out of the tube for analysis or detection.

basicPropertyValues.val: Dynamic headspace analysis of a flowing sample solution in the form of a thin film on the surface of a heated tube.
Equilibrium system containing two or more solvents forming two phases with a single interface.

comments: The analyte(s) are usually metal ions.

The chelating agent replaces water molecules in the coordination sphere of the metal ions. Consequently, the resultant metal chelates have a hydrophobic character which facilitates their transfer to the organic phase.

basicPropertyValues.val: Extraction method wherein charged analytes are extracted from an aqueous phase into an organic phase, assisted by a chelating agent.
Coacervative extraction at a temperature above the cloud point temperature.

comments: In cloud point extraction a small volume "surfactant-rich" phase enriched in sample components of moderate water solubility and a bulk aqueous phase with dissolved surfactant and highly water-soluble compounds are formed.

basicPropertyValues.val: Extraction by a surfactant-rich, water-immiscible phase formed by adding a dehydrating agent to a colloidal solution of the sample and a surfactant above its critical micelle concentration.

comments: Continuous liquid-liquid extraction techniques are used when the sample volume is large, the distribution constant is small, or the rate of extraction is slow.
Typical apparatuses are shown below.

Typically, a fixed volume of extraction solvent is recycled through the aqueous sample solution by distillation and condensation, and dripped into the sample solution. A siphon mechanism allows continuous recovery of the extraction solvent based on its relative density.

basicPropertyValues.val: Extraction in which a water-immiscible extraction solvent is continuously percolated through an aqueous solution and returned to the extraction solvent reservoir.Apparatus for continuous liquid–liquid extraction with a lighter-than-water extraction solvent (left) and a heavier-than-water extraction solvent (right). In each case the extraction solvent is contained in the round bottom flask and the aqueous sample in the vertical glass column.

comments: The Craig CCD apparatus consists of a battery of glass vessels designed to allow the mixing, settling, and transfer of extracted phase (sample) and the addition of fresh solvent (extractant) in a repetitive fashion. Movement about the horizontal axis provides gentle mixing of the phases, settling, and decanting of the upper phase. The extraction process is slow but is fully automated.

basicPropertyValues.val: Apparatus for extraction based on a multistage countercurrent distribution.
Extraction comprising a cascading series of states where the raffinate is brought into a subsequent stage and contacted with fresh solvent.
Type of continuous multistage extraction equipment in which there is only one interface at which phase separation by settling occurs.

comments: The dispersion solvent is typically a polar organic solvent miscible with water.

basicPropertyValues.val: Solvent used to disperse the extraction solvent as fine droplets throughout the sample solution in dispersive liquid–liquid microextraction.

comments: The extraction phase can be formed by ion exchange when an ionic liquid is used as the extraction solvent.
The extraction phase is formed by a mixture of extraction and dispersion solvents injected into the sample solution.
The extraction phase is sedimented by centrifugation and collected for analysis.

basicPropertyValues.val: Extraction of analyte(s) from an aqueous solution by fine droplets of extraction phase dispersed throughout the solution.
Liquid-liquid distribution process that involves the transfer of ionic species from the extractant to the aqueous phase in exchange for ions from the aqueous phase.
Microextraction technique using a liquid as the extraction phase.
Multistage countercurrent separation based on a discontinuous, differential migration process employing stepwise extraction.

comments: The extraction solvent with a volume typically \(\pu{\lt 50 \upmu L}\) is suspended as a drop from the tip of a microsyringe needle as shown in the figure below.

The sample is stirred or agitated during extraction. After extraction, the drop of acceptor phase is collected by withdrawing it into the syringe used to support the drop for the final analytical measurement.

Typically, the sample is aqueous and the acceptor phase is an organic solvent, resulting in a two-phase extraction system (\(\ce{aqueous\!->\!organic}\)). SDME can also be operated in three-phase mode (\(\ce{aqueous\!->\!organic\!->\!aqueous}\)), or in the headspace mode (\(\ce{aqueous\!->\!gas\!->\!organic or aqueous}\)).

basicPropertyValues.val: Extraction of analytes from the gas phase or solution by a single drop of extraction solvent.Typical experimental arrangement for single-drop microextraction.
Droplet of organic solvent recovered from the surface of the sample solution by solidification induced by cooling.

comments: The extraction solvent has a melting point near room temperature to facilitate collection after solidification induced by cooling. The solidified solvent is then melted and analysed.

basicPropertyValues.val: Microextraction employing a solidified floating organic drop.
Physically distinct part of an extraction process in which transfer of analyte(s) occurs, followed by phase separation.

comments: There are the same number of phase separation interfaces as there are stages.

basicPropertyValues.val: Type of continuous multi-stage liquid-liquid distribution equipment in which each stage has a physically distinct cycle of interphase contact and separation.
Distribution in a biphasic system formed by two aqueous solutions containing structurally incompatible components (two polymers or a polymer and a salt) above a critical concentration.

comments: A typical workflow scheme for matrix–solid-phase dispersion is shown in the figure below.
For additional sample clean-up the sorbent/sample mixture is deposited at the head of a solid-phase extraction cartridge containing a suitable sorbent to retard the elution of matrix components.

basicPropertyValues.val: Extraction in which samples are blended with an abrasive solid sorbent, forming a free flowing powder from which target analytes are recovered by solvent elution.Typical work flow scheme for solid-phase matrix dispersion. (i) Sample is blended with an abrasive sorbent, (ii) free flowing powder containing sample is packed in a short column, and (iii) target analytes are recovered by elution.

comments: Microwaves are electromagnetic radiation of \(\pu{300\!{–}\! 300,000 MHz}\). They heat the extraction solution by their interaction with dielectric compounds (solvent or sample). Microwave heating is more efficient and rapid than convection and conduction and enhances the migration rate of compounds into the extraction solvent. Microwave-assisted extraction may be performed in a closed vessel with control of temperature and pressure or in an open vessel at atmospheric pressure.

basicPropertyValues.val: Leaching using microwave energy to heat the solvent in contact with the sample or the sample directly.

comments: Instrument requirements are similar to pressurized-liquid extraction.
The solvation properties of water become closer to organic solvents at elevated temperatures.

basicPropertyValues.val: Extraction by water below its critical point (\(\pu{374.15^{\circ}C}\) and \(\pu{22.064 MPa}\)).

comments: A typical apparatus is shown in the figure below.

The sample, in the form of a fine powder or liquid supported on an inert solid, is packed into an extraction vessel and inserted in a flow-through system. The temperature, pressure, solvent type, and static and/or dynamic extraction time are varied to optimize the extraction performance.

basicPropertyValues.val: Leaching performed at elevated temperature and pressure.Schematic diagram of a typical apparatus for pressurized-liquid extraction. Gas flow is used to displace the extraction solvent from the sample chamber.

comments: A typical apparatus for classical Soxhlet extraction is shown in the figure below.
The extraction solvent is cycled in a continuous-discrete process by distillation, condensation and siphoning. Extracted material accumulates in the distillation flask.

basicPropertyValues.val: Leaching with fresh solvent cycled multiple times through a fine solid sample contained in a porous thimble.Typical apparatus for classical Soxhlet extraction.

comments: The most common supercritical fluid for extraction is carbon dioxide (critical point = \(\pu{39.9^{\circ}C}\) and \(\pu{73.8 bar}\)). Its extraction properties are varied by changing its density (temperature and pressure) or by addition of polar organic solvents.

The powdered sample, or supported liquid, is packed into a vessel and extracted using static or dynamic extraction conditions. The extracted material is typically recovered by reducing the pressure of the extraction fluid, allowing it to evaporate.

basicPropertyValues.val: Use of a supercritical fluid to extract analytes from a solid or supported liquid sample.

nodes.lbl: QuEChERS (quick, easy, cheap, effective, rugged and safe) extraction

comments: Often used for samples containing pesticide residues.
The general procedure includes micro-scale extraction with acetonitrile, salt-assisted phase separation, and sample clean up using dispersive solid-phase extraction.
There are several procedural variations of the general method for application to particular compounds or sample matrices.

basicPropertyValues.val: Streamlined multiresidue method for extraction and clean-up of analytes in complex matrices.

comments: Ultrasound energy causes cavitation in solvents, which generates numerous tiny bubbles in liquids and mechanical erosion of solids, including particle rupture. It promotes digestion and slurry formation with solids and homogenization and emulsification with liquids.
Ultrasound energy is applied to samples in a vessel immersed in a water bath or applied more directly using devices, such as horns, probes, or sono-reactors.

basicPropertyValues.val: Extraction in which ultrasound energy is used to increase the extraction rate by enhancing the contact area between the sample and solvent and by promoting efficient agitation.

comments: Acid digestion can also be used to remove a matrix constituent by selective volatilization, e.g. silicon by the use of hydrofluoric acid.
Acid digestion can be performed in closed or open vessels.

basicPropertyValues.val: Process in which the sample (analyte and matrix) is dissolved by an acid.

comments: The increased rate of decomposition and retention of volatile trace elements is an advantage over open-vessel acid digestion.

basicPropertyValues.val: Type of acid digestion performed in a closed vessel at elevated pressure.
Sample dissolution with simultaneous matrix simplification.
Type of bomb acid digestion with microwave radiation used for sample heating.
Type of acid digestion performed at ambient pressure wherein the digestion temperature is limited by the boiling point of the acid.

comments: Typical samples are sea water, waste water, drinking water, or fresh water.

basicPropertyValues.val: Formation of free metal ions in aqueous solution by oxidation under the influence of UV light and possibly an oxidizing agent (e.g. hydrogen peroxide or peroxodisulfate) in order to break down dissolved organic matter and metal complexes.

comments: The particles are sized to allow sample processing by gravity, gentle suction or low pressure.

basicPropertyValues.val: Short disposable column containing a bed of porous particles immobilized between two porous frits.

comments: Principal roles include removal of contaminants from the sorbent bed to create the conditions for a stable flow of the sample solution during sampling and to facilitate wetting of hydrophobic sorbent surfaces before applying aqueous samples.

basicPropertyValues.val: Small volume of solvent used to prepare the sorbent for efficient sample processing.
Small volume of strong solvent used to displace target analytes from the sorbent bed.

comments: Foamed polyurethane sorbents have a minor use for extracting compounds from water.
Their main attribute is their favourable aerodynamic properties, which permit sampling at high flow rates.

basicPropertyValues.val: Sorbent consisting of spherical, micron-sized, agglomerated particles bound together in a rigid and highly porous structure used for the extraction of semi-volatile organic compounds from air in high-volume samplers.

comments: A high level of selectivity is possible due to the specificity of antibody-antigen spatial fitting and interactions.
The porous support is chosen to minimize nonspecific matrix interactions to facilitate processing complex biological, environmental and food samples without additional clean up.

basicPropertyValues.val: Porous material with surface bound monoclonal or polyclonal antibodies capable of selective extraction of target analytes by formation of reversible antibody-antigen (compound) binding complexes.

comments: Compounds with hydrogen-bonding or ionic functional groups are extracted efficiently, while neutral dipolar compounds are extracted to a lesser extent and weakly polarizable compounds to a limited extent.
Typical inorganic oxide adsorbents include silica gel, alumina, magnesium silicate (Florisil), and zirconia.

basicPropertyValues.val: Adsorbent with site-specific polar and ion exchange functional groups that extract analytes from a gas or liquid phase by their complementary interactions with the surface.

comments: Ion-exchange sorbents are usually classified as weak or strong depending on the identity of the ionic group and whether its charge is independent of the sample \(\rm{pH}\) (strong ion-exchanger) or can be varied by changing the sample \(\rm{pH}\) (weak ion-exchanger).
Ionic or ionizable compounds are extracted almost exclusively from water by electrostatic interactions with ion-exchange sorbents.

basicPropertyValues.val: Porous sorbent material  containing fixed ionic sites with a complementary charge to that of the target analyte(s).

comments: From the gas phase compounds are extracted by non-polar and weakly polar interactions with high surface area sorbents.
Low-specificity sorbents have surfaces with a low concentration of polar functional groups and retain compounds mainly through non-selective dispersion interactions.
Typical low-specificity sorbents are chemically-bonded porous silica, hydrophobic macroporous polymers, and various forms of carbon.

basicPropertyValues.val: Sorbent with a non-selective surface used almost exclusively to extract analytes from an aqueous solution. The sorbent has a largely passive role in the extraction, with the driving force being the expulsion of the organic contaminants from waterto minimize disruption of the water structure.

comments: Magnetic nanoparticles have a high surface area-to-volume ratio and a low mass. They are easily dispersed in solution. A magnet facilitates recovery of the nanoparticles from the sample solution or suspension.

basicPropertyValues.val: Sorbent consisting of nanometre-sized, spherical particles with a magnetic or magnetisable core surrounded by a sorbent shell.

comments: The dual extraction mechanism allows fractionation of mixtures into a neutral and acidic fraction and a basic fraction by a stepwise change in \(\pu{pH}\) of the eluting solvent.

basicPropertyValues.val: Porous sorbent material with surface co-bonded ion exchange and alkyl functional groups.

comments: The imprint is obtained by the co-polymerization of functional and crosslinking monomers in the presence of a template molecule (the analyte) and a porogen. The resultant imprint possesses a steric (size and shape) and chemical (spatial arrangement of complementary functional groups) memory of the template molecule that enable the sorbent to selectively rebind the template molecule from a complex matrix.

basicPropertyValues.val: Porous polymer sorbent with synthetic recognition sites with a high specificity for the sorption of a targeted compound or group of structurally-related compounds.

comments: Multiwell plates typically contain 24, 96, 256, or 384 wells with volumes varying from about \(\pu{100 \upmu L}\) to \(\pu{10 mL}\). They are used for parallel sample processing in high throughput applications.
The design of a typical multiwall extraction plate is shown in the figure below.

basicPropertyValues.val: Regular array of wells in a single moulded body with a short sorbent bed or disc embedded at the base of each well.Multiwell extraction plate.

comments: Vertical movement of the plunger allows bidirectional flow of sample through the sorbent bed (active sampling). Alternatively, sampling can occur by diffusion of analytes into the syringe needle (passive sampling).

basicPropertyValues.val: Gas-tight syringe with a sorbent-filled needle.

comments: Small discs are self-supporting while larger discs require external support.

basicPropertyValues.val: Suspension of micron-sized sorbent particles woven into a glass fibre matrix.

comments: For general use the flexible discs are supported on a sintered glass disc in a filtration apparatus using suction to generate the desired flow through the membrane.

basicPropertyValues.val: Suspension of micron-sized sorbent particles distributed throughout a web of poly(tetrafluroethylene) microfibrils formed into a thin disc of various diameters.

comments: Access to the retentive interior surface is restricted for macromolecules by a physical or chemical diffusion barrier that facilitates elution of macromolecules and extraction of low-mass compounds.
The restricted access barrier can be accomplished by size exclusion, differential partitioning, or other phenomenon.

basicPropertyValues.val: Porous material with a biocompatible outer surface and a retentive interior surface.

comments: An optional step, intermediate between sample application and elution.

basicPropertyValues.val: Weak solvent used to displace matrix components from a sorbent without displacing the target analyte(s).

comments: Typical uses of solid-phase extraction include isolation, concentration, solvent exchange, and matrix simplification.

basicPropertyValues.val: Extraction of analytes from a gas, liquid, or fluid by transfer to a solid sorbent.
Use of a solvent, typically combined with agitation, to remove target analytes from a sorbent.

comments: A micropipettor is used to control sample processing steps. This arrangement facilitates the use of bidirectional flow (the cycling of sample and solvents across the sorbent bed in either direction) for sample processing.
A typical design of sorbent-containing pipette device for high throughput sample processing is shown in the figure below.

basicPropertyValues.val: Disposable pipette tip with a small packed bed, disc, or monolithic plug of sorbent at its narrow end.Sorbent containing pipette tips in an array for use with a multiwall sample plate.

comments: The tape is typically a suitably-sized sheet of poly(dimethylsiloxane) polymer, or a piece of particle-loaded membrane, with a large surface area-to-volume ratio.

basicPropertyValues.val: Extraction from the surface of a solid by sorbent or polymer film in the form of a tape in direct contact with, or in the headspace above, the sample.

comments: Rapid stirring accelerates mass transfer overcoming some of the limitations of diffusion controlled mass transfer in sessile solutions.
Related devices for simultaneous stirring and sampling include rotating disc, stir rod, and stir membrane devices.

basicPropertyValues.val: Extraction of compounds from solution by a sorbent coated magnetic stir bar by rapid stirring (direct immersion) or by exposure to the headspace above a sample (headspace extraction).

comments: Extracted ions are recovered by elution with a solution of complexing agent with a higher binding constant than the surface-bound macrocyclic ligand.

The selectivity of the extraction process depends on the stability of the host-guest complex, which can be optimized for individual ions by the choice of the macrocyclic cavity and the type of donor atoms.

basicPropertyValues.val: Porous sorbent with surface-bound macrocyclic ligands designed for the extraction of metal ions and some anions from aqueous solution.

comments: Extraction occurs at a basic \(\pu{pH}\) for compounds with hydrogen-donating functional groups on neighbouring carbon atoms (1,2- and 1,3-). The analytes are released by elution with an acidic aqueous-organic solvent solution.

basicPropertyValues.val: Porous sorbent with surface-bound phenylboronic acid groups for the selective extraction of bifunctional compounds by reversible formation of 5- or 6-membered covalent cyclic boronic acid complexes.
Extraction by a matrix-compatible immersion solid-phase microextraction device where the extraction phase and support are chosen to eliminate matrix interferences.

comments: This technique is typically used as a 96-blade brush in conjunction with a multiwell sample plate.

basicPropertyValues.val: Solid-phase microextraction device where the extraction phase (sorbent) is dispersed in the form of a thin coating on the surface of a blade.
Solid-phase microextraction in the fibre format with a sorbent temperature maintained below that of the sample matrix during extraction.
Extraction phase in the form of a thin layer supported on a fibre made of inert material, such as fused silica, stainless steel, or nickel-titanium alloy.
Solid-phase microextraction where the extraction phase is placed in the headspace above the sample.
Solid-phase microextraction where the extraction phase is immersed directly into the sample.
In-tube format device with a sorbent-coated capillary placed inside a needle.
Extraction utilizing a coated open tubular or packed capillary tube as the extraction phase in a flow system.

comments: Sorption of particles and macromolecules by the extraction phase is a potential source of interference in the extraction process or subsequent determination of analytes when sampling occurs by direct contact of the extraction phase with the sample. In some cases this can be addressed by incorporation of specific properties in the extraction phase that minimize matrix-extraction phase interactions for problem matrix components.

basicPropertyValues.val: Immersion solid-phase microextraction where the extraction phase is designed to minimize sorption of particles or macromolecules present in the sample matrix.

Immersion solid-phase microextraction in which the extraction phase is surrounded by a permeable membrane that allows access of analytes to the extraction phase while shielding the extraction phase from matrix components with a potential to interfere in the extraction or subsequent analysis.

comments: Particles are typically of a nanometre size and applied in the dispersion mode of extraction.

basicPropertyValues.val: Extraction phase in the form of sorbent particles.

comments: Facilitates more rapid stirring than conventional sorbent-coated stir bars (see stir bar sorptive extraction) without deterioration of the sorbent coating, because it is not in contact with the vessel wall.

basicPropertyValues.val: Sorbent-coated disc consisting of a polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) base with an integrated magnet and a sorbent film attached to one side.
Solid-phase microextraction in which the extraction phase is coated on the internal surface of a needle.

comments: The extraction phase can also be a liquid physically coated on a fiber or wire support.

This term is often narrowly used to describe an extraction process employing a syringe-based sampling device with a short length of small gauge solid fiber or wire coated with sorbent attached to one end of the plunger of the syringe to facilitate bidirectional movement of the sorbent-coated fiber (wire) through the syringe needle for extraction, storage, and desorption of extractants. For extraction the sorbent is exposed to the headspace above the sample or immersed directly into the sample solution. Sample components diffuse into and/or onto the sorbent coating until equilibrium is reached. The extractants are subsequently recovered by thermal desorption into a gas stream (typically in the liner of an injection port of a gas chromatograph) or rinsed from the sorbent coating with solvent for determination by other methods.

basicPropertyValues.val: Microextraction where the extraction phase is a solid.
Solid-phase microextraction where the sorbent is in the form of a thin film on a support or self supported membrane.

comments: A typical experimental arrangement is shown in the figure below.
Electromembrane extraction is typically performed in three-phase mode (\(\ce{aqueous\!->\!organic\!->\!aqueous}\)).
The sample is agitated or stirred during extraction.

basicPropertyValues.val: Hollow-fibre liquid-phase microextraction in which the extraction is driven by an electrical potential sustained between the sample solution and the acceptor phase, separated by a supported liquid membrane.Typical experimental arrangement for electromembrane extraction of cations (anions extracted by reversing the polarity). SLM, supported liquid membrane in the form of a porous hollow fiber with solvent-filled pores.

comments: The internal diameter of the tube is typically \(\pu{500 \upmu m}\) – \(\pu{1.5 mm}\) with walls \(\pu{100 \upmu m}\) to \(\pu{300 \upmu m}\) thick. Fibers are typically prepared from porous poly(propylene), although other materials can be used.

basicPropertyValues.val: Narrow cylindrical tube prepared from a porous polymer.

comments: A typical experimental arrangement is shown in the figure below.

The acceptor phase can be aqueous, which provides a three-phase extraction system (\(\ce{aqueous\!->\!organic\!->\!aqueous}\)), or an organic solvent, providing a two-phase extraction system (\(\ce{aqueous\!->\!organic}\)).
The sample is agitated or stirred during extraction.
The supported liquid membrane is generally an organic solvent immiscible with water and the sample an aqueous solution.

basicPropertyValues.val: Liquid-phase microextraction of analytes from a liquid (or gaseous) sample by a supported liquid membrane in the form of a porous hollow fibre with solvent-filled pores. The analytes are transferred to an acceptor phase contained in the cavity of the hollow fibre.Typical experimental arrangement for hollow-fiber supported liquid membrane (SLM) for liquid-phase microextraction.
Extraction of analytes from a sample by permeation through a membrane.

comments: MESI is typically used in a system consisting of three components: (1) membrane extraction module; (2) sorbent interface; and (3) gas chromatograph. A flow of gas is used as the stripping phase to transfer permeate to the sorbent trap for concentration and thermal desorption into the gas chromatograph.

basicPropertyValues.val: Membrane extraction with a sorbent trap for concentration of the permeate.

comments: Microdialysis is performed mostly in a living biological system.

basicPropertyValues.val: Dialysis by a short length of hollow-fibre membrane used for sampling.
Membrane in which permeation occurs by processes other than flow through pores.

comments: PALME is usually performed in the three-phase mode (\(\ce{aqueous\!->\!organic\!->\!aqueous}\)).
The solvent-filled filter pores function as a supported liquid membrane typically based on an organic solvent immiscible with water.

basicPropertyValues.val: Extraction of analytes from aqueous samples in a multiwell plate with a porous membrane at the base of each well by migration through the solvent-filled membrane pores into an acceptor phase located in each well.

comments: Perfusate is also used to describe the stripping phase in dialysis.

basicPropertyValues.val: Stream of extraction phase entering a dialysis module.
Process by which mass transfer occurs through a membrane.
Membrane in which permeation occurs through its porous structure.
Sample left over in membrane separations after initial contact with the membrane.

comments: Typically, a membrane filled with acceptor phase and formed into a sealed tube is immersed in the sample. As a passive sampling device, it is used to obtain time-weighted average concentrations for trace contaminants or to isolate them for toxicity assessment. With triolein as an acceptor phase, it is used to estimate the bioconcentration of contaminants in fatty tissues of organisms.

basicPropertyValues.val: Membrane extraction in which the membrane fully encloses an acceptor phase.
The sample in membrane separations prior to contact with the membrane.
Extraction phase in a membrane separation.

comments: Porous polymeric hollow fibres and filter disks are typically used as support formats for microextraction techniques.
Water immiscible organic solvents are typically employed in the preparation of supported liquid membranes.
The extraction phase is typically collected in an automated fraction collector and introduced into a detector via a robotic device.

basicPropertyValues.val: Flow system with extraction device employing a local detector.
Extraction in a mechanical device regulated by feed-back of information without human intervention.
Extraction according to manually preselected conditions without further human intervention.

comments: A typical workflow for bead injection in a flow manifold is shown in the figure below.

basicPropertyValues.val: Fully renewable (disposable) packed sorbent bed for solid-phase extraction in a flow manifold or mesofluidic platform using programmable flow extraction.Bead-injection protocols for automated solid phase microextraction with sorbent renewal for each assay [Reproduced from  https://www.flowinjectiontutorial.com].a) Injection of a metered amount of particles or beads with reactive surfaces in the flow system followed by mechanical trapping or capture with the aid of external energy sources; b) Injection of a metered volume of sample; c) Interaction of analyte(s) with sorptive surfaces; d) Preconcentration of analyte(s) followed by detection of native species or derivatization products; e) Automatic removal of sorptive surfaces.

comments: Also termed environmental availability.
Bioaccessibility tests are usually performed by operationally defined leaching.

basicPropertyValues.val: Fraction of analytes desorbed from a sample potentially available to organisms.
Leaching of analytes from a solid or semi-solid sample in a flow-through device to evaluate their bioaccessibility.

comments: The forced flow of matrix or extraction phase is controlled by an external device.

basicPropertyValues.val: Extraction by flow of sample through or over the extraction phase, or vice versa, to enhance the extraction rate.
Continuous optical interrogation of a packed-sorbent bed in a flow system at any stage of the extraction process prior to analyte elution and sorbent regeneration.
Coupling of a flow system with extraction device to a detector without flow interruption.
Batch-type extraction in which the barrel of a syringe pump is used as the device for liquid-phase microextraction or dispersive solid-phase microextraction.
Automatic batch-type liquid-phase microextraction by sequential injection analysis using an external extraction container (e.g. pipette tip) connected to a multiposition rotary valve.
Microfluidic platform containing microconduits to facilitate extraction processes with pressure-driven or electroosmotic flow.
Mesofluidic platform containing microconduits for extraction processes mounted on a multi-position rotary valve.
Extraction using a device with at least one movable part that replaces or supplements human effort in any (or all) steps of the process.

comments: Lab-on-valve platforms belong to the group of mesofluidic devices.

basicPropertyValues.val: Extraction device with channel widths from \(\pu{10 \upmu m}\) to \(\pu{2 mm}\) integrated into a flow platform.
Miniaturized flow injection analysis device for extraction with conduits of a diameter greater than \(\pu{0.1 mm}\).
Extraction device with channel widths from \(\pu{100 nm}\) to \(\pu{10 \upmu m}\) integrated into a flow platform.
Programmable flow extraction device with microsolenoid valves for processing microliter sample volumes.

comments: A suitable discontinuous interface is a rotary valve with a sample loop.

Hernia of a part of the stomach through a rupture of the diaphragm at the esophageal opening.

comments: Herpes viruses cause several infections, all characterized by blisters and ulcers, including chickenpox, shingles, genital herpes, and cold sores or fever blisters.

basicPropertyValues.val: Family of viruses including herpes simplex types 1 and 2, and herpes zoster (also called varicella zoster).

Short-term in vivo procedure in which the androgenic or antiandrogenic effects of a test substance are studied in castrated, peripubertal male rodents, as indicated by changes in the weights of androgen-dependent tissues.
Structural component of the limbic system of the vertebrate brain involved in short-term and long-term memory and spatial navigation.
Absence of nerve ganglia throughout all or part of the gastrointestinal tract, causing dysregulation of intestinal motility.
Presence of excessive bodily and facial hair.

comments: This results in varying degrees of mental impairment and abnormal development of eye, nose, and lip.

basicPropertyValues.val: Birth defect in which the embryonic forebrain fails to divide completely to form the cerebral hemispheres.
Any of a class of closely similar DNA sequences occurring in various genes and involved in regulating pattern formation, segmentation, and morphogenesis during embryonic development in many species.
Replacement of part of one segment of an insect or other segmented animal by a structure characteristic of a different segment, especially through mutation.

Having the same relationship, relative position, or structure. (Of organs) Similar in position, structure, and evolutionary origin but not necessarily in function. (Of chromosomes) Pairing at meiosis and having the same structural features and pattern of genes. (Of a series of chemical compounds) Having the same functional group(s) but differing in structure by a fixed group of atoms.
Crossing over between two similar or identical strands of DNA, resulting in exchange of corresponding stretches of DNA between two sister chromosomes.
Procedure in which larvae of the honey bee (Apis mellifera) are exposed to a test chemical in the diet and subsequent mortality is recorded daily up to the \(\pu{72\!\!{-}\!h}\) \(\pu{LD_{50}}\).
Substance formed in one organ or part of the body and carried in the blood to another organ or part where it selectively alters functional activity.

comments: HGP also involved studying the genome of a number of organisms other than humans, including insects, fish, plants, and other mammals.

basicPropertyValues.val: International research project that started in 1990 with the goal of determining the base-pair sequence of the human genome. The project was declared complete in 2003.

comments: The abnormal tissue typically results from gene expression from paternally derived chromosomes and a loss of maternal chromosomes.

basicPropertyValues.val: Vesicular or polycystic mass resulting from the proliferation of the trophoblast, with hydropic degeneration and avascularity of the chorionic villi.
Rare condition in which the brain’s cerebral hemispheres are replaced by sacs filled with cerebrospinal fluid.
Accumulation of serous fluid in a sacculated cavity; specifically, such an accumulation in the space of the tunica vaginalis testis, or in a separate pocket along the spermatic cord.
Accumulation of excess cerebrospinal fluid within the ventricles of the brain; head enlargement and brain damage may occur.

comments: Hydronephrosis may be a congenital deformity or the consequence of an obstruction in the ureter.

basicPropertyValues.val: Swelling of the funnel-shaped part of the kidney, where urine is collected to enter the ureter.
Gross edema of the entire body, with severe anemia, occurring in hemolytic disease of the newborn.
Dilation of a ureter with fluid.
Accumulation of fluid in a sac, cyst, or bursa.
Thin, membranous fold of highly variable appearance that, before its rupture, partly occludes the opening of the vagina.
Second pharyngeal or branchial arch of the developing embryo, from which different tissues around the neck, ear, and face will develop.
Ventral to the long axis of the body.
Extension of a limb or part of a limb beyond the normal limit.
Flexion of a limb or part of a limb beyond the normal limit.
Abnormal multiplication or increase in the number of normal cells in a tissue or organ.
Abnormally wide space between two organs, especially referring to the eyes.
Enlargement of an organ or tissue as a result of the increase in the size of its cells.
Innermost of the three primary germ layers, adjacent to the blastocyst cavity, that develops into the endoderm.

comments: Primary hypogonadism refers to a defect that is inherent in the gonad while secondary hypogonadism refers to a defect lying outside the gonad, often an endocrine effect.

basicPropertyValues.val: Inadequate functioning of the testes or ovaries as manifested by deficiencies in gametogenesis or in secretion of gonadal hormones.
Underdevelopment or atrophy of a tissue or organ.
Birth defect in which the urethra opens on the underside of the penis, or into the vagina.

Region at the base of the brain containing specialized nerve cells that help activate, control, and integrate peripheral autonomic mechanisms, endocrine activities, and some somatic functions such as body temperature, sleep, and appetite.
Abnormally low dioxygen content or tension. Deficiency of dioxygen in the inspired air, in blood, or in tissues, short of anoxia.
Congenital disorder of keratinization, characterized by dryness and scaling of the skin, often associated with other defects and with abnormalities of lipid metabolism.

Twins resulting from one zygote that, at an early stage of embryonic development, separated into two independently growing cell aggregations giving rise to two individuals of the same sex and identical genetic constitution.
Relating to the ileum and the cecum.
Third portion of the small intestine, between the jejunum and the cecum.
Congenital absence of an anal opening due to the persistence of epithelial plug (persistence of the anal membrane) or to complete absence of the anal canal.
Embedding of the early embryo in the lining of the uterus.

comments: Quantitation of imposex in the dog whelk (Nucella lapillus) has been used to monitor pollution by the antifouling agent tributyltin oxide (TBTO) in marine environments.

basicPropertyValues.val: Pseudohermaphroditic condition in female gastropods (snails) manifested by the development (imposition) of male characteristics such as a penis or vas deferens.

comments: Imprinting is an epigenetic modulation of gene expression, thought to be regulated by attachment of methyl groups to the DNA, and by chromatin structure.

basicPropertyValues.val: Differential expression of a gene, depending on whether it was transmitted through the sperm or the egg.

Strain of an animal that has been inbred by brother-sister matings for more than \(\pu{20}\) generations, and consequently all the individuals of the strain are more than \(\pu{98\%}\) genetically identical.

comments: This index measures the female’s ability to become pregnant and may be used as a general indicator of fertility.

basicPropertyValues.val: In rodents, number of pregnant females divided by the number of females mated, multiplied by 100.
In rodents, number of females with live born offspring divided by number of females with evidence of pregnancy, multiplied by \(\pu{100}\).

comments: This index measures the male’s ability to produce sperm that are capable of impregnating a female, assuming all mated females are fertile.

basicPropertyValues.val: In rodents, number of males impregnating females divided by number of males mated, multiplied by \(\pu{100}\).
Percentage of seminiferous tubules containing identifiable spermatogonia.
Pluripotent stem cell that is generated from an adult cell by genetic reprogramming.
Persistent inability of either a male or a female to achieve conception or to produce offspring.
Anatomical funnel-shaped opening, often referring to the hollow stalk that connects the hypothalamus and the posterior pituitary gland, or to the portion of the Fallopian tube that receives the ovum.
Passage in the lower anterior abdominal wall, which in men conveys the spermatic cord and in women the round ligament of the uterus.

Any of a group of peptide hormones secreted by the follicular granulosa cells of the ovary and the Sertoli cells of the testis, inhibiting follicle-stimulating hormone secretion by the anterior pituitary.
Malformation producing a cranial defect at the occiput, with the brain exposed, often combined with a cervical rachischisis and retroflexion.
Delivery of sperm into the female reproductive system for the purpose or with the result of causing pregnancy.
Any of a family of cell membrane glycoproteins that mediate cell-to-cell and cell-to-extracellular matrix interactions.

comments: Most types of intermediate filaments are cytoplasmic, but one type, the lamins, is nuclear.

basicPropertyValues.val: Any of a group of fibrous proteins (including keratin fibres, neurofilaments, desmin, and vimentin) that make up part of the cytoskeleton of most eukaryotic cells; so named because, at about \(\pu{10 nm}\) diameter, they are intermediate in thickness between actin filaments and microtubules.
Condition of having both male and female characteristics: thus, the state of being intermediate between the sexes.
Infertility treatment in which the sperm is injected through the membrane of the egg into its cytoplasm.

comments: Intramembrous ossification is one of two mechanisms of bone formation, the other being endochondral ossification.

basicPropertyValues.val: Creation of bone tissue during fetal development of jawed vertebrates, as well as during the healing of bone fractures; the tissue forms from mesenchymal stem cells residing in an extracellular matrix devoid of collagen.

comments: Growth restriction can be due to maternal or fetal causes, as well as to malnutrition and toxic exposures.

basicPropertyValues.val: Subnormal, poor growth of the fetus.

comments: The intrinsic and extrinsic pathways converge with cleavage of procaspase 3 by either caspase 8 (extrinsic pathway) or caspase 9 (intrinsic pathway).
This pathway involves the release of pro-apoptotic proteins from the mitochondria.

basicPropertyValues.val: Apoptotic pathway of cell death initiated from within the cell by signals initiated by mitochondrial damage and (or) DNA damage, a defective cell cycle, detachment from the extracellular matrix, hypoxia, loss of cell survival factors, or other types of severe cell stress; characterized by the activation of caspase 9.
Rearrangement of a chromosome in which, after breakage at two points, a segment is reversed, resulting in a change in sequence of nucleotides.
Fertilization outside the body, used as a treatment for infertility.
Local deficiency of blood supply, and hence of dioxygen, to an organ or tissue, caused by constriction or obstruction of the blood vessels.

comments: Intake during pregnancy has a high teratogenic risk.

basicPropertyValues.val: Vitamin A-like medication (13-cis retinoic acid) used, among other things, for acne treatment.
Second part of the small intestine between the duodenum and ileum.
Dissolution of a cell nucleus, especially during mitosis and meiosis but also following necrosis.
Irreversible fragmentation of the nucleus of a dying cell following karyolysis, whereby its chromatin is distributed irregularly throughout the cytoplasm.

Characterization of the number, form, and size of the chromosomes of an individual or a species. Photomicrograph of an individual’s chromosomes, arranged according to a standard classification for the species.
Fibrous protein forming the main structural constituent of hair, feathers, hoofs, claws, horns, etc.
Replacement of the outer epithelial layer of cells, especially in skin, with keratin-rich structures.
Acidosis, as in diabetes, pregnancy, or starvation, accompanied by the accumulation of ketone bodies in body tissues and fluids.

comments: Ketone bodies tend to accumulate in the blood and urine of individuals affected by starvation or uncontrolled diabetes mellitus.

basicPropertyValues.val: Ketone that is an intermediate product of the breakdown of fats in the body; any of three compounds, acetoacetic acid, acetone, and (or) \(\upbeta\)-hydroxybutanoic acid, found in excess in blood and urine of persons with metabolic disorders.

Syndrome in males resulting from a genetic defect in which an extra female X chromosome (thus an XXY genotype) is present in a male, characterized by small testes, long legs, enlarged breasts, reduced sperm production, and mental retardation.
Mutation that leads to the loss of function of a particular gene.
Rearward curvature or convexity of the spine in excess of normal, resulting in a protuberant upper back.
Physical efforts of expulsion of the fetus and the placenta from the uterus during birth.
Secretion of milk from the mammary gland, usually to feed the infant during the neonatal period.
Time following pregnancy during which the mammary glands secrete milk.
Layer of connective tissue, underlying the epithelium of a mucus membrane, containing capillaries and lymphatic vessels, as well as fibroblasts and cells of the immune system.
Part of the respiratory tract between the pharynx and the trachea, having walls of cartilage and muscle and containing the vocal cords.

comments: Thalidomide is used as a therapeutic drug and thalidomide-associated embryopathy occurs in regions where leprosy is endemic.

basicPropertyValues.val: Disease caused by infection with the bacterium Mycobacterium leprae, often affecting the skin and nerves and causing body parts to become deformed.
Malformation characterized by an abnormally tall, narrow cranium.

comments: Unlike albinism, where the defect is in the production of melanin pigment only, animals with leucism usually have pigment in the eye, as retinal pigment cells do not derive from the neural crest.

basicPropertyValues.val: Lack of pigmentation in the skin, hair, or feathers as a result of a failure of pigment cells to develop, or to migrate to those locations from their origin in the neural crest, in the embryo.
Abnormally low concentration of white cells (leukocytes) in the blood.
Normal position of the heart in the left hemithorax with the apex pointed to the left, and transposition of other viscera.
Cell in the testis that produces androgens, mainly testosterone, in the presence of luteinizing hormone.
Fibrous remnant of the ductus arteriosis linking the aortic arch and the top of the left pulmonary artery.
Embryonic outgrowth of mesoderm covered in ectoderm that will give rise to one of the forelimbs or hindlimbs.
Technique that studies patterns of heredity in high-risk families, in order to locate a disease-causing gene mutation by identifying co-inherited traits, usually by producing a LOD score.

Occurrence in members of a population of combinations of linked genes in non-random proportions, implying that the genes are close enough together on a chromosome to make it unlikely that they will be separated by recombination (see homologous recombination) during meiosis.
Disorder of fat metabolism characterized by the accumulation of abnormal levels of certain lipids in the body.
Multiple offspring produced by a mammal from one pregnancy.
Specific location of a gene or DNA sequence on a chromosome.

comments: An LOD score of 3 or greater is considered indicative of genetic linkage with odds greater than \(\pu{1000\!{:}\! 1}\).

basicPropertyValues.val: Ratio of the likelihood of two or more loci remaining together when chromosomes recombine (true linkage) to the likelihood of this occurring by chance alone.

comments: Some degree of lumbar curvature is normal. Excessive curvature (lumbar hyperlordosis) is sometimes called swayback.
This posture is also associated with a rodent being in heat.

basicPropertyValues.val: Forward (ventral) curvature of the spine in the lumbar and cervical regions.
Piercing into the subarachnoid space of the lumbar region in order to obtain spinal fluid for diagnostic purposes or to inject a drug.
Phase of the human menstrual cycle, usually lasting \(\pu{14 days}\), beginning with formation of the corpus luteum and ending, in the absence of fertilization, with the onset of menstruation.
Hormone made by the pituitary gland that acts on the ovary to control egg maturation and to trigger ovulation. The same hormone acts in the testes to trigger production of testosterone.
Relating to lymph or its secretion.

comments: Lymphoid tissue occurs throughout the body in lymph nodes, thymus, tonsils, and spleen.

basicPropertyValues.val: Relating to or denoting tissue responsible for producing lymphocytes and antibodies.

comments: The Barr body, visible in some female cells, is an inactivated X chromosome.
The Lyon hypothesis was designated the Lyon law by the European Molecular Biology Organization (EMBO) in 2011.
This phenomenon leads to mosaicism for X-linked genes in the female, since the paternal X chromosome is inactivated in some cells and the maternal one in others.

basicPropertyValues.val: Hypothesis (named after Mary Lyon) that random inactivation of all but one X chromosome occurs in each female mammalian cell in early development, thus explaining why the effect of the X chromosome on phenotype is the same in males with one copy as in females with two copies.

One of a group of rare inherited metabolic disorders resulting from a defect in lysosomal function, commonly a deficiency of enzymes required for the metabolism of lipids, glycoproteins, or mucopolysaccharides, resulting in their accumulation in the cell.
Congenital disorder characterized by an abnormally large head and (or) brain.
